docs.text:

This matrix consolidates the domain authority, host permissions, permitted MCP servers, and absolute constraints for each of the 14 canonical Pantheon agents in OpenCode.

docs.title: 1. Decision Flowchart: Who to Call?
docs.text:
Use this visual decision guide to pick the right specialist for your objective:

flowchart TD
    Start(["🎯 What is your objective?"]) --> Type{Task Type}

    Type -->|"Large feature / Multiple files"| Zeus["⚡ @zeus (Orchestrator)"]
    Type -->|"Architecture / Planning first"| Athena["🏛️ @athena (Architect)"]
    Type -->|"Small bug / Typo / Surgical edit"| Talos["⚡ @talos (Hotfix Express)"]
    Type -->|"Backend / API / Business Logic"| Hermes["✉️ @hermes (Backend TDD)"]
    Type -->|"Frontend / React / CSS / A11y"| Aphrodite["🎨 @aphrodite (Frontend UX)"]
    Type -->|"Database / SQL / Migrations"| Demeter["🌾 @demeter (Database)"]
    Type -->|"Pre-PR audit / Tests / Security"| Themis["⚖️ @themis (Auditor)"]
    Type -->|"Docker / CI/CD / GitHub Actions"| Prometheus["🔥 @prometheus (DevOps)"]
    Type -->|"Investigate code without modifying"| Apollo["🔍 @apollo (Read-Only)"]

    Zeus -->|"Delegates planning"| Athena
    Athena -->|"Code research"| Apollo
    Zeus -->|"Dispatches implementation"| Hermes & Aphrodite & Demeter & Prometheus
    Hermes & Aphrodite & Demeter -->|"Submits for audit"| Themis

docs.title: 3. What Each Agent CAN and CANNOT Do
@zeus (Orchestrator)
docs.text:
• CAN: Decide task flow, dispatch specialists, arbitrate uncertainties via Jev (pantheon_jev_decide), discover project skills (pantheon_skill_search), prompt human decisions (question), read up to 50 lines for fast routing.
  • CANNOT: Edit code directly (edit: deny), execute commands in terminal (bash: deny), ask user to run terminal commands, or perform broad recursive scans across .git/** or node_modules/**.

docs.title: @athena (Architect)
docs.text:
• CAN: Create architectural specs, analyze trade-offs, define implementation blueprints and detailed technical plans (PLAN.md).
  • CANNOT: Implement or edit code (edit: deny), run tests/shell (bash: deny), or prompt approval dialogs within the child session (always hands the plan back to Zeus).

docs.title: @hermes (Backend)
docs.text:
• CAN: Write FastAPI/Node endpoints, business logic, unit tests in TDD, run testing and linting commands via bash.
  • CANNOT: Mutate database schemas (delegates to @demeter), create visual UIs (delegates to @aphrodite), or configure Docker/CI pipelines (delegates to @prometheus).

docs.title: @aphrodite (Frontend)
docs.text:
• CAN: Create React/Next components, style with Tailwind/CSS, enforce WCAG accessibility, run dev servers and UI tests (Vitest/Playwright).
  • CANNOT: Implement backend routes or persistence schemas, or ignore accessibility contrast guidelines.

docs.title: @demeter (Database)
docs.text:
• CAN: Create and migrate schemas (Alembic/Prisma), optimize SQL queries, prevent N+1 queries, assert referential integrity.
  • CANNOT: Touch frontend components or implement business logic outside data persistence.

docs.title: @themis (Auditor)
docs.text:
• CAN: Run test suites and linters in read-only evaluation mode (Biome, ruff, pytest), issue compliance verdicts (PASS, PASS_WITH_NOTES, BLOCK, BLOCK_INTENT).
  • CANNOT: Modify files or fix issues found (edit: deny absolute — strict separation of powers).

docs.title: @prometheus (DevOps)
docs.text:
• CAN: Maintain Dockerfile, docker-compose, GitHub Actions workflows, build/deploy scripts, monitoring configurations.
  • CANNOT: Implement feature code or business logic.

docs.title: @talos (Hotfixer)
docs.text:
• CAN: Fix localized bugs, typos, missing imports, and micro-edits directly in a single turn without TDD ceremony.
  • CANNOT: Execute architectural refactoring or high-risk multi-file tasks.

docs.title: @apollo (Investigator)
docs.text:
• CAN: Search codebase with grep, glob, and read, fetch external documentation with webfetch, synthesize structured findings.
  • CANNOT: Modify files (edit: deny), run arbitrary terminal commands (bash: deny).

docs.title: @mnemosyne (Memory Bank)
docs.text:
• CAN: Read and update markdown files strictly inside .pantheon/memory-bank/ and record approved ADRs.
  • CANNOT: Touch files outside .pantheon/ (e.g. README.md is updated by @hermes or @talos).

docs.title: 4. Subagents and Jev Arbitration
docs.text:
By default, only the @zeus orchestrator invokes pantheon_jev_decide. Specialists can be explicitly authorized by setting the environment variable:

export PANTHEON_JEV_SPECIALIST_CALLERS="athena,hermes,aphrodite,apollo"

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
🇧🇷 Versão em Português disponível: Leia em Português

Audience: developers extending Pantheon and anyone who wants to know how the pieces fit. Setup is in Installation; user-facing 2.x behavior is in OpenCode 2.x.

docs.title: Agent flow
docs.text:
Pantheon replaces the single-agent coding loop with a conductor and specialists.

flowchart TD
    User(["👤 User Request"]) --> Zeus["⚡ Zeus (Conductor)"]

    Zeus -->|"Planning"| Athena["🏛️ Athena (Plan)"]
    Zeus -->|"Discovery"| Apollo["🔍 Apollo (Discovery)"]
    Zeus -->|"Hotfix (Express)"| Talos["🛡️ Talos (Hotfix)"]
    Zeus -->|"Memory Management"| Mnemosyne["🧠 Mnemosyne (Memory)"]
    Zeus -->|"Git/GitHub PRs"| Iris["🌈 Iris (GitHub)"]

    Athena -.->|"Approved Plan"| Zeus
    Zeus -->|"Implementation"| Specialists

    subgraph Specialists["🛠️ Implementation Specialists"]
        Hermes["✉️ Hermes (Backend)"]
        Aphrodite["🎨 Aphrodite (Frontend)"]
        Demeter["🌾 Demeter (Database)"]
        Prometheus["🔥 Prometheus (Infra)"]
        Hephaestus["🔨 Hephaestus (AI Pipelines)"]
        Nyx["🌙 Nyx (Observability)"]
        Gaia["🌍 Gaia (Remote Sensing)"]
    end

    Specialists -->|"Material & Sensitive Changes"| Themis["⚖️ Themis (Review & Audit)"]
    Themis -->|"PASS Verdict"| Zeus
    Zeus -->|"Delivery & Summary"| User

Zeus orchestrates but never implements. He routes bounded work to one specialist and adds planning, discovery, parallel work, and review when scope and risk call for them. /pantheon-deepwork is the checkpointed workflow for heavy multi-phase work. The canonical agent files live in src/agents/*.md; Agents & Skills indexes them.

The quality gates are qualitative, not file/line thresholds: self-contained work stays inline; one bounded specialist task goes to one agent; independent fronts may use separate root dispatches. Themis reviews material and sensitive changes — auth, security, data/schema, and anything that changes behavior broadly. See Permissions, Gates & Delegation.

docs.title: Delegation mechanics
docs.text:
Pantheon delegates through the host's native child-session engine. The callable tool is subagent in the reported root runtime; host/API documentation calls the same mechanism task(). Tool availability, background options, and completion observability are properties of the active runtime, not of Pantheon. The former pantheon_delegate tool and its delegation engine were removed.

Every root dispatch carries a concise handoff brief: objective/result, bounded scope and acceptance criteria, only the relevant inputs, constraints and safety gates, expected deliverable and return format, and verification. Do not copy the full conversation or unrelated history.

Return contracts are role-specific:

Caller Return format Implementation agent ## subtask_summary with files, summary, tests, blockers Investigation (apollo) Structured findings: bullets, paths with line numbers, snippets ≤3 lines Planner (athena) The complete Markdown plan, never a summary or a pointer Council specialist ## specialist_response

Delegated work gets at most one retry after an initial transient failure. When no completion/status tool is exposed, prefer synchronous dispatch or wait for a host notification; do not assume polling, cancellation, job tracking, or board-based recovery.

On OpenCode 2.x, the plugin additionally enforces a caller/target matrix for Pantheon-managed subagent requests when the host exposes ctx.permission.hook. It matches the permission source's session, message, and tool-call ids to a short-lived record from tool.execute.before, then requires the host session to have no parentID. Missing, stale, replayed, or mismatched origins fail closed. If the hook is unavailable, host permissions remain in control. The matrix itself is documented in Permissions, Gates & Delegation.

docs.title: What the plugin registers
docs.text:
There is a single generation: 2.0 removed the V1 plugin line, and the surface below is the only one.

The plugin is registered under the plural plugins key as the <installed>/src/plugin directory. src/plugin/index.ts re-exports the real entry at src/plugin.ts; the tool-hook registration in src/plugin.ts is fed by the tool definitions in src/pantheon/tools.ts.

Four unconditional tools:

  • hashline_edit — src/pantheon/tools.ts
  • pantheon_cost — src/pantheon/tools.ts
  • pantheon_model — src/pantheon/tools.ts
  • pantheon_local_decision — src/pantheon/tools.ts. The advisory local selector; it rejects execution unless the host tool context identifies the caller as Zeus.

Up to two host-dependent tools:

  • vision_describe — added only when ctx.model.list is a function (src/plugin.ts; definition at src/pantheon/native-vision.ts).
  • pantheon_bounded_read — added only when the tool.execute.before hook registered and the host exposes the permission and session APIs (src/plugin.ts; definition at src/pantheon/bounded-read.ts). Root Zeus sessions only.

The three goal tools are absent because the goal loop needs infrastructure the host's PluginContext does not expose. The gap is reported as goal-tools.

The plugin also wires five event subscriptions (session.created, session.idle, session.deleted, session.error, session.compacted), session hooks (prompt, context, compaction), a read-only-enforcing execute.before hook (the same handler denies the orchestrator read/glob/grep of source, tests and scripts), an execute.after chain (task-result-guard → context-sandbox → read-enhancer → formatter + delegation audit), and a permission.evaluate hook when the host exposes it. The entry constructs the idle todo enforcer itself when the host's session domain exposes what it needs; where it does not, the gap is reported as idle-todo-enforcer.

sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant Host as OpenCode 2.x Host
    participant Plugin as Pantheon Plugin
    participant Guard as Execute Guards
    participant Agent as Specialist Agent

    Host->>Plugin: tool.execute.before
    Plugin->>Guard: Read-only guard (blocks Zeus from direct source/test reads)
    Guard-->>Host: Allow / Deny
    Host->>Agent: Execute tool or subagent
    Agent-->>Host: Return raw tool output
    Host->>Plugin: tool.execute.after
    Plugin->>Guard: task-result-guard → context-sandbox → read-enhancer
    Guard-->>Host: Sanitized, bounded and enriched result

docs.title: Installer and config model
docs.text:
Canonical sources in src/ are read by the installer and written into the target config. There is no runtime generation step.

  • The installer writes opencode.json, never opencode.jsonc. A host may merge a sibling .jsonc; see Compatibility.
  • It strips Pantheon references from the legacy singular plugin key and the plural plugins key before writing the current registration, so two Pantheon plugins never coexist. Legacy V1-shaped config keys are normalized to the 2.x shapes before the write.
  • Third-party plugin and MCP entries are preserved and never converted.
  • A versioned per-file ownership inventory records what the installer owns, so reconcile can find stale, unchanged installer files.

The package exposes the plugin as the importable export pantheon-opencode/plugin; the pantheon-opencode/local-decision-router subpath is the decision-router TypeScript source. There is no bridge export and no second contract: the plugin works standalone with graceful degradation.

docs.title: Memory and context stores
docs.text:
Pantheon has three separate stores, documented once in Memory:

  • pantheon-memory — durable SQLite entries with FTS5/BM25 keyword search.
  • pantheon-persistence — session checkpoints and manual session goals.
  • .pantheon/memory-bank/ — human-reviewed project files, read on demand.

They are not synchronized. MCP tool availability depends on the active agent's grants; namespaces are organizational filters, not access-control boundaries.

docs.title: MCP entrypoints
docs.text:
Five local Python stdio servers, declared in scripts/install-mcp.mjs:74-78 and registered at :196-301:

Server Entrypoint pantheon-resources scripts/mcp_resources.py pantheon-code-mode scripts/code_mode.py pantheon-memory scripts/memory_mcp.py pantheon-persistence scripts/mcp_persistence.py pantheon-vision src/mcp/pantheon_vision.py

The entrypoints were renamed away from the shared *_server.py token; the installer heals stale paths using the mapping in scripts/install/config-migration.mjs:521. Setup and allowlists are in MCP.

docs.title: Design principles
docs.text:
• One home per fact. The support matrix, installer mechanics, release process, and benchmark evidence each live in exactly one page.
  • Configuration plus a thin runtime. Agent behavior lives in Markdown (src/agents/*.md, src/instructions/*.instructions.md, src/skills/*/SKILL.md); the installed plugin supplies orchestration, tools, and guards.
  • Fail closed on identity and permissions; fail open on presentation. A malformed permission origin denies the delegation. A malformed compaction payload leaves the message array untouched.

docs.title: Branch Protection: main
docs.text:
🇧🇷 Versão em Português disponível: Leia em Português

Why this matters: Branch protection prevents force-pushes, requires passing CI checks before merge, enforces linear history, and ensures no one (not even admins) can bypass the pipeline. Without it, the agent orchestration pipeline (Iris → Themis → merge) is just a suggestion, not a guarantee.

docs.title: Enable Protection via GitHub UI
docs.text:
1. Go to your repo on github.com → Settings → Branches (sidebar).
  2. Click Add branch protection rule (or Add rule).
  3. In Branch name pattern, enter: main
  4. Enable the following checkboxes:

docs.title: ✅ Required Settings
docs.text: Setting Checkbox label Why ✅ Require a pull request before merging All changes go through a PR reviewed by Themis/Iris ✅ Require approvals — set to 1 At least one reviewer must approve ✅ Dismiss stale pull request approvals when new commits are pushed Re-review after changes ✅ Require status checks to pass before merging Block merge if CI fails ✅ Require branches to be up to date Prevents merge skew

docs.title: 🔍 Required Status Checks
docs.text:
Add these exact check names (they match real workflow jobs; GitHub reports the job id when a job has no name: override):

  • validate
  • test-suite
  • plugin-ts-coverage
  • commitlint
  • security-scan
  • CodeQL

version-check is not a check. That job was folded into validate. There is no PR Checks workflow in this repository; do not add PR Checks / label-by-title or PR Checks / recommend-version.

Applying protection is a manual maintainer action. No workflow changes branch protection and an agent must not do it.

Tip: Type each name in the search box and select it. GitHub will auto-suggest matching check names once the workflow has run at least once on main.

docs.title: 🔒 Additional Protections
docs.text: Setting Checkbox label Value ✅ Require linear history — (on) — Prevents merge commits, keeps history clean ✅ Include administrators — (on) — Even admins must follow the rules ❌ Allow force pushes — (off) — Never allow force pushes ❌ Allow deletions — (off) — Never allow branch deletion

docs.title: 🚀 Apply Rule
docs.text: Click Create (or Save changes).

docs.title: Alternative: gh CLI
docs.text:
If you prefer the command line, use the GitHub CLI to apply the same settings:

gh api repos/:owner/:repo/branches/main/protection \
  --method PUT \
  --field required_status_checks='{
    "strict": true,
    "checks": [
      {"context": "validate"},
      {"context": "test-suite"},
      {"context": "plugin-v2-ts-coverage"},
      {"context": "commitlint"},
      {"context": "security-scan"},
      {"context": "CodeQL"}
    ]
  }' \
  --field enforce_admins=true \
  --field required_pull_request_reviews='{
    "required_approving_review_count": 1,
    "dismiss_stale_reviews": true
  }' \
  --field required_linear_history=true \
  --field allow_force_pushes=false \
  --field allow_deletions=false

Note: Replace :owner with your GitHub username or org (ils15) and :repo with pantheon-opencode. You need admin or write permissions on the repo to run this command. Run it only after every required check has passed on main; see the pre-flight checklist below.

docs.title: MANDATORY pre-flight checklist
docs.text:
If a required check never passes, every push to main is locked out, including the release pipeline. Confirm all of the following before the PUT:

  • [ ] (a) All six checks exist as workflow jobs: validate, test-suite, and plugin-v2-ts-coverage in ci.yml; commitlint in commit-lint.yml; security-scan in security-scan.yml; and CodeQL analysis in codeql.yml.
  • [ ] (b) They all pass on current main (or a PR), including the push run on main. If any fails, fix the workflow first — never enable protection on a failing check.
  • [ ] (c) Only then apply the PUT, and verify with gh api repos/ils15/pantheon-opencode/branches/main/protection.

docs.title: Admin bypass
docs.text:
The command above sets enforce_admins=true. If the repository owner needs an escape hatch to unblock the release pipeline, set it to false initially and restore it after two stable releases:

gh api -X PATCH repos/ils15/pantheon-opencode/branches/main/protection \
  -F enforce_admins=true

docs.title: Grandfather policy
docs.text: Commitlint is enforced from this point forward on all new commits (local .husky/commit-msg hook plus the CI commitlint job). Commits before 2026-08 are grandfathered; they are never rewritten or retroactively linted. git log -15 --format=%s | npx --no commitlint will list them as violations; that output is expected. New commits must follow Conventional Commits.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
After enabling protection, verify it's active:

gh api repos/ils15/pantheon-opencode/branches/main/protection --jq '.required_status_checks.checks[].context'

Expected output: 

[
  "validate",
  "test-suite",
  "plugin-v2-ts-coverage",
  "commitlint",
  "security-scan",
  "CodeQL"
]

You can also check the GitHub UI: Settings → Branches → main rule shows a green "Protection enabled" badge.

docs.title: How This Enforces the Agent Pipeline
docs.text:
┌─────────────────────────────┐
                              │  User pushes to feature/    │
                              │  branch                     │
                              └──────────┬──────────────────┘
                                         │
                                         ▼
                              ┌─────────────────────────────┐
                              │  Iris opens Draft PR        │
                              │  → validate, test-suite,    │
                              │    plugin-v2-ts-coverage,   │
                              │    commitlint, security-scan│
                              │  → CodeQL analysis          │
                              └──────────┬──────────────────┘
                                         │
                                         ▼
                              ┌─────────────────────────────┐
                              │  All status checks pass?    │
                              │  ─── NO ───→ Fix & re-push  │
                              │  ─── YES ───↓               │
                              └──────────┬──────────────────┘
                                         │
                                         ▼
                              ┌─────────────────────────────┐
                              │  Themis reviews & approves  │
                              └──────────┬──────────────────┘
                                         │
                                         ▼
                              ┌─────────────────────────────┐
                              │  User says "merge"          │
                              │  → Iris merges (squash)     │
                              │  → Linear history preserved │
                              └─────────────────────────────┘

Without branch protection, any of these steps can be skipped by a force-push or a direct commit to main. Enable it once and never worry about it again.

docs.title: Compatibility and Support Policy
docs.text:
🇧🇷 Versão em Português disponível: Leia em Português

This page is the only home of the support policy, the host gate rules, the Node floor, and the known-issue list. Other pages state the support summary once and link here.

docs.title: Supported hosts
docs.text:
Support is declared for an OpenCode family, not for individual minors. A minor does not need its own measurement to be supported.

  • OpenCode 2.x — supported. Every 2.x minor is supported, including minors released after this document was written. 2.0 removed the OpenCode V1 contract entirely: the package registers only the host-native plugin surface described in Architecture.
  • Known broken: OpenCode 2.0.22. It does not expose ctx.permission.assert (src/plugin.ts; bench/results/p05-permission-matrix-2026-10-22.md:169), so Pantheon's permission-ordering and bounded-read paths fail there. The host loader also requires the plugin entry to be a directory (scripts/install/opencode.mjs); the installer already writes that form for every 2.x host, so it is not a 2.0.22-specific failure. Do not install Pantheon on 2.0.22.
  • Node.js >=26.4.0 is the package floor; Python >=3.11 is required for the optional MCP servers. The node:sqlite >=22.5 threshold for pantheon_cost is a capability threshold, not the package floor.
Pantheon line OpenCode 1.19.x OpenCode 2.x OpenCode 2.0.22 1.7.x — last line with V1 support Supported — V1 plugin Supported — the plugin Known broken — not supported 2.0 and later Not supported Supported — the plugin Known broken — not supported

A missing measurement is not a support gap. The plugin targets the OpenCode 2 contract and degrades feature by feature when a host lacks an optional domain; it does not require a per-minor blessing. The evidence table below lists the hosts that happen to have a record in this repository.

docs.title: Node runtime floor
docs.text:
Pantheon declares engines.node as >=26.4.0, its own alignment policy with the official OpenCode Node build that CI pins to exactly 26.4.0. Node 22, Node 24, and Node 26.0–26.3 are outside the supported range.

This package floor does not imply that every OpenCode host runs on Node. Official OpenCode 2.x ships a Bun runtime path and a separate Node build pinned to Node 26.4.0, so the host runtime you choose does not move Pantheon's package floor. No Bun minimum is asserted.

Below the floor the package still installs, but postinstall only warns and skips the TUI and config sync, and the CLI stops with an explicit version message before any setup write. The optional pantheon_cost SQLite backend has a separate, lower capability threshold — node:sqlite on Node >= 22.5 — which does not lower the package or CLI support floor.

docs.title: The host gate
docs.text:
There is exactly one contract to write, and the installer must CONFIRM the host is OpenCode 2.x before any file is written. There is no generation to select and no fallback: an install decision made on an unconfirmed host would be a guess, and guessing is the defect the gate exists to prevent. The gate lives in scripts/install/opencode-version.mjs and resolves in this order:

  1. An explicit OPENCODE_VERSION=v2 environment pin skips the probe entirely. It exists so CI, sandboxes, and operators can make the answer deterministic without a runnable host binary. v1 (or any other value) is refused — v1 gets the unsupported-host message, anything else an invalid-value error.
  2. An OPENCODE_BIN basename of opencode2 is an explicit operator hint and always resolves to 2.x.
  3. A --version probe of the host binary. The probe runs inside a throwaway HOME/XDG sandbox (5-second budget on an apply, 2-second on a dry run — plan and apply must make the SAME decision), captures stdout and stderr, and anchors on the tool name: a version token immediately preceded by opencode is the host's own version, so a runtime token ahead of it (node v22.1.0 (opencode 2.0.29)) or a trailing build date (opencode v2.0.29 built 2026.10.04) cannot flip the answer. A major the gate refuses to interpret (0, or a calendar-year value) is reported, not read.

Every refusal happens before any write:

  • major === 1 — a confirmed 1.x host is a fact, not a detection gap: the plugins registry this installer writes would be silently ignored there.
  • probe failed / unreadable / unparseable / contradictory — the installer cannot confirm the one premise it writes for, so it refuses loudly instead of guessing.

In every refusal case the message names the deterministic escape hatch: OPENCODE_VERSION=v2. An operator whose opencode is a wrapper that prints a bare path is indistinguishable from a real host by construction; the remedy is the env pin, not a heuristic.

docs.title: Config registration and the host's config merge
docs.text:
Pantheon registers its plugin in opencode.json. The installer reads and writes only that file — it never reads, writes, or edits a sibling opencode.jsonc.

An OpenCode 2.x host also loads opencode.jsonc from the same config directory when one exists and merges the two files: scalars from the .jsonc win, and arrays are unioned. A plugin/plugins entry in .jsonc therefore joins the effective plugin set instead of replacing the registration Pantheon wrote, and the merge is silent. What the installer guarantees is narrower than "the effective set is correct": if both files exist, it warns and names both paths, because anything in the .jsonc — including a stale Pantheon entry — is outside what it can see. Resolve that by moving the entries you want into opencode.json and deleting the .jsonc.

Within opencode.json the installer strips Pantheon references from both the legacy singular plugin key and the plural plugins key, then registers only the current entry, so a host never loads two Pantheon plugins. The singular plugin key is legacy: a third-party entry found there that the host could actually load is additionally registered under the plural plugins key (and reported), because the 2.x host does not read the singular key and the entry would otherwise stop loading silently. Legacy V1-shaped config keys (agent, permission, flat mcp, …) are normalized to the 2.x shapes before the write.

docs.title: Historical note: OpenCode 1.19.x (removed in 2.0)
docs.text:
2.0 requires OpenCode 2.x. The V1 plugin line was removed. Of its old registrations, only stale references are still recognized, for cleanup: a singular plugin key entry and a src/plugins/pantheon-hooks.ts path are stripped or migrated, never registered — the hooks file no longer exists in this package, and src/plugin.ts today is the entry of the one remaining plugin, not a V1 identity.

The V1 surface is kept here for history: it registered six tools (hashline_edit, the three pantheon_goal_* tools, pantheon_cost, pantheon_model), the BackgroundJobBoard lifecycle, the V1 event/tool hooks, and the V1 compaction path.

On OpenCode 1.19.4, with bash, write, and edit set to deny and read set to allow, the host makes bash and write unavailable, produces no side effect, and read still works. The proof is config-level, not hook-based: the probe recorded zero permission.ask invocations. The permission request goes to the client instead (permission.asked, GET /permission, then POST /permission/{id}/reply), and a client reject does block the call.

docs.title: The OpenCode 2 path
docs.text: The 2.x path is the only path: it registers tools with input/output schemas, event subscriptions, session hooks, a read-only-enforcing execute.before hook (which also denies the orchestrator read/glob/grep of source, tests and scripts), and — when the host exposes it — a permission.evaluate delegation-matrix hook. It is not full V1 feature parity: the three goal tools remain unsupported and are reported as goal-tools, as are the host-domain gaps the seed names (idle-todo-enforcer, tool-ceiling, todo-restore, board-transitions). See Architecture for the contract and OpenCode 2.x for user-facing behavior.

docs.title: Verified versions (evidence)
docs.text:
This table is evidence, not the boundary of support. It lists only hosts with a measurement recorded in this repository. A 2.x minor absent here is still supported; it is simply unmeasured.

Host Contract Evidence 1.19.4 V1 (historical) bench/results/p05-permission-matrix-2026-10-22.md 2.0.29 2.x bench/results/p05-permission-matrix-2026-10-22.md; bench/results/f4a-v229-admission-identity-2026-10-14.md 2.0.30 2.x bench/results/p05-permission-matrix-2026-10-22.md 2.1.0 2.x bench/results/p05-permission-matrix-2026-10-22.md 2.1.2 2.x bench/results/p05-permission-matrix-2026-10-22.md; docs/internal/validation.md 2.1.3 2.x bench/results/p05-permission-matrix-2026-10-22.md

The table above is a measurement record, not a release checklist. A new 2.x minor is supported on release day; measuring it is optional evidence work.

docs.title: End of life and known issues
docs.text:
1.7.x is the last Pantheon line that supports an OpenCode 1.X host. From 2.0 onward the line drops the V1 contract and requires OpenCode 2.x. This is a Pantheon support boundary, not a claim that 1.7 lacked OpenCode 2 support.

  • OpenCode 2.0.22 is known broken. It does not expose ctx.permission.assert, so the permission-ordering and bounded-read paths cannot run there. It is the only known-broken host in the supported family.
  • A supported host is not required to have a measurement row. The table above is evidence; the supported family is the boundary.

docs.title: Pantheon Installation Guide — 2.0 (OpenCode 2.x)
docs.text:
🇧🇷 Versão em Português disponível: Leia em Português

Pantheon 2.0 requires OpenCode 2.x — the OpenCode V1 contract was removed entirely (1.7.x was the last line with V1 support). There are two complementary ways to install. Loading the plugin through the host's native flow is the recommended path; npx pantheon-opencode init remains the installer for the full component set. pantheon_model offers only manual status, show, set, and reset, with no preset wizard: the host default stays intact without an explicit per-agent override, and preset markers and PANTHEON_MODEL_PRESET are ignored and preserved. Without an override, delegates inherit the parent chat model natively.

docs.title: TL;DR (Quick Start)
docs.text:
# Recommended: load the plugin through the host (npm package; a git URL works too)
opencode plugin add pantheon-opencode

# Full component set: agents, skills, instructions, commands, plugins (+ MCP/TUI)
npx pantheon-opencode init

# Headless preview; add --yes to authorize applying the same defaults
npx pantheon-opencode init --headless
npx pantheon-opencode init --headless --yes

# Separate repository wrapper: config migration review + installer preflight
npm run setup

# Verify installation
npm run doctor

# Development & Testing Prerequisites:
# Run `npm install` first! Unit and contract test suites (`npm run test:quick`,
# `npm run test:node`, `npm run test:ts`) require devDependencies (tsx, biome,
# esbuild) to avoid silent UNMET DEPENDENCY failures.
npm install

# Optional: activate the Jev decision model in the same pass
npx pantheon-opencode init --decision-model opencode-console-jev/jev-1.13 --decision-monthly-usd 5 --decision-per-decision-usd 0.10
  • Requirements: a supported host — OpenCode 2.x (Pantheon 2.0 does not support an OpenCode 1.x host) — plus Node.js >=26.4.0 for Pantheon's CLI/installer/Node tooling and Python 3.11+ (optional, MCP servers).
  • Known broken: OpenCode 2.0.22 does not expose ctx.permission.assert. Node 22, Node 24, and Node 26.0–26.3 are outside the supported range.
  • The host-native plugin flow. opencode plugin add <npm-package|git-url> records the plugin under the plural plugins key as an object entry ({ "package": …, "options": { … } }). The host also auto-discovers every directory under .opencode/plugins/ in the project and the global config directory. A local path must be a DIRECTORY containing an index.ts/ index.js — a file path warns "must be a directory" and a symlink is ignored. Pantheon's npm package is pantheon-opencode; its plugin export is pantheon-opencode/plugin. See Compatibility for the supported family and the known-broken exception.
  • Components. npx pantheon-opencode init installs agents, skills, instructions, commands, and the plugin registration + TUI (plugins component) by default; runtime (Python/MCP) and prompts are opt-in via selection or --components. A TTY run selects components and target, shows the plan, then requests one final authorization with default no. Without a TTY, init only previews unless --yes is supplied; --yes suppresses prompts but still shows the preview and performs the integrity/drift checks.
  • Direct init and npm run setup are different entry points. npm run setup runs the config review before installer init. Config migration and installer changes are both preflighted before one final authorization; --yes does not replace it. This wrapper is separate from direct init.
  • The setup stage inspects $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/opencode/opencode.json and $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/opencode/opencode.jsonc separately when XDG_CONFIG_HOME is set to an absolute path; otherwise it uses ~/.config/opencode (the global init target). Direct global init uses the same target resolver. Relative XDG_CONFIG_HOME values are rejected before writes. The host layers these files in order: opencode.json then opencode.jsonc; later scalar values win, plugin and permission arrays append, and MCP servers merge by name with the later whole server object replacing the earlier one. Other fields follow the host's field-specific merge behavior; there is no universal array-union rule. The review treats each file as a separate layer, never deletes either file, and never silently selects one. Interactive users select the target file(s) and choose a policy source when permission values conflict; the setup wrapper then shows the redacted policy and installer summaries before its final authorization. Legacy permission rules can be prepared as native permissions; MCP ask cannot be enforced on this host, so the user must explicitly choose an outcome (allow, deny, leave accessible without a rule, or disable a nested MCP server where supported). Verified Pantheon-owned plugin/MCP entries are reported; JSONC entries move only when order and same-name overrides remain safe. An unsafe managed plugin blocks setup. For an unsafe managed MCP entry, interactive setup offers Continue, leaving those entries unchanged or Abort setup. Continuing keeps the entry in JSONC (where its whole server object can override the JSON layer); if init would also seed that server and create a duplicate layered entry, setup blocks before writes. Inspect and reconcile the layered config when that check blocks. Flat third-party MCP entries in opencode.jsonc are not rewritten by the installer, so setup blocks before consent or writes and reports only a redacted key path and count. Convert them manually to mcp.servers or remove them before retrying. Already nested third-party servers remain untouched.
  • --yes alone authorizes no npm run setup writes. Headless/CI/non-TTY setup runs are preview-only and do not invoke writing init, even with --yes. --dry-run previews the migration and invokes init's dry-run only. Direct npx pantheon-opencode init --headless --yes does authorize its own apply. JSONC files with comments inside values that would be rewritten are preview-only rather than serialized lossily. Applied files receive a verified backup set under <config-dir>/.pantheon/backups/<timestamp>/ and per-file atomic replacements; the writer preserves the existing permission mode. Ownership, group, ACLs, and extended attributes are not preserved or guaranteed. A partial failure may leave earlier file replacements applied; multiple files are not applied atomically. To locate a setup backup, inspect the timestamped entries under <config-dir>/.pantheon/backups/; use pantheon-opencode restore to review and recover from a backup set.
  • With npm's default configuration, mismatched versions can emit EBADENGINE as a warning during install. Pantheon's postinstall then skips Node/config sync and lets the package finish installing; the CLI blocks configuration with an explicit message before writing files.
  • engine-strict=true can make npm itself stop the install. To switch without a global/system-wide install, use a user-managed Node version manager:

nvm install 26.4.0 && nvm use 26.4.0
# or: fnm install 26.4.0 && fnm use 26.4.0
# or: volta install node@26.4.0
- This does not assume a universal Node runtime for the OpenCode host: official OpenCode 2.x — a supported host — has a Bun runtime path and a separate Node build pinned to Node 26.4.0. - That host runtime does not change the package floor, and no Bun minimum is declared. - node:sqlite >=22.5 is only a capability threshold for the optional pantheon_cost backend, not the package's support requirement. - In an interactive TTY setup summary, the installer recommends a persistent external location for future worktrees: <project-parent>/.pantheon-worktrees/<exact-repository-directory-basename>/<task> (for example, /home/user/.pantheon-worktrees/My Project/feature-name). Use the project directory's exact basename, including spaces; do not normalize it into a slug. - The recommendation is guidance for agents only; Pantheon does not create Git worktrees or directories automatically. - Interactive TTY init uses Clack prompts for one component selection and one global/project target, then shows the preview and requests final authorization (default no). --yes suppresses prompts; runtime and prompt templates remain opt-in in either mode. - Every path that ends without applying prints exactly one line naming where it stopped (canceled at the review prompt, declined at the install location, canceled at the component selection, …). Ctrl-C is handled after the install starts and until its outcome is recorded: before a managed write it exits 130 without changing configuration; after a write it records partial with applied: true, warns that changes may be partial, preserves the backup, and does not roll back automatically. The handler is deactivated once apply is recorded, so Ctrl-C during optional post-install --doctor cannot rewrite a completed install. While a prompt is on screen, the prompt library also turns Ctrl-C into the matching cancel. A cancel, decline, failure, or apply is written to .pantheon/last-run.json in the selected target; install-state.json is written by apply. Pre-authorization and drift refusals keep their no-write guarantee. A run-record write failure is reported as a warning and never changes the exit code. - Delegation and background mode depend on the tools exposed by the host version/runtime. In the reported Beta 10 session, Zeus had the subagent tool, with no task_status/cancel_task or guarantee of tracking/recovery. - Check the runtime's schema and documentation; do not assume task() or background are available. The experimental variable below applies only to hosts/versions that document it. - 5-minute walkthrough: QUICKSTART.md.

docs.title: Installer review, authorization, and recovery
docs.text:
init --dry-run shows the managed-file operations without applying them. To review in one invocation and authorize in another, save a versioned plan:

# Human-readable or JSON preview (stdout only)
npx pantheon-opencode init --project --no-mcp --components agents --dry-run
npx pantheon-opencode init --project --no-mcp --components agents --dry-run --json

# Save and apply the reviewed plan; without --yes, a TTY session asks
npx pantheon-opencode init --project --no-mcp --components agents --dry-run \
  --save-plan .pantheon-install-plan.json
npx pantheon-opencode init --apply-plan .pantheon-install-plan.json --yes

The artifact is versioned JSON written atomically with 0600 permissions; it stores identities, options, snapshots/fingerprints, and operations, not the contents of generated files. It is bound to the plan's original path, target, and package identity. On apply, the installer recomputes the plan and compares source and destinations; on drift it aborts before writing (exit code 3). --apply-plan accepts only the plan path and authorization (--yes/-y or a TTY prompt). Saved plans with --force/--clean are not supported.

A dry run runs the same host gate as the apply, including the --version probe, which executes inside a throwaway HOME/XDG sandbox with a 2-second timeout, so the preview writes nothing and cannot disagree with the apply it authorizes. A host the gate cannot confirm as OpenCode 2.x refuses the preview exactly like the apply; OPENCODE_VERSION=v2 is the deterministic escape hatch when no host binary can be probed. The plan carries v2_capabilities (what the plugin registers, plus the statically known not-registered seed and the scope of that list) and plugin_options (whether the written plugin entry can receive the opt-in options), so a machine sees the same facts the text notice prints. A sibling opencode.jsonc that the installer neither reads nor writes is reported in the plan's advisories array. The plan describes managed-file operations and, when runtime is selected, names whether the virtual environment will be created, reused, or recreated and that MCP dependencies may be installed/downloaded. It does not enumerate every dependency. Per-file detail is opt-in via --verbose (or structured --json). postinstall/sync-tui is also outside the init approval flow and may update TUI artifacts without a prompt. Do not treat the preview as a transaction or as a promise of automatic rollback.

Before the first managed write, init creates an exact backup under .pantheon/backups/<timestamp>/ (directory 0700, files 0600, retaining the 5 most recent). Because the backup is byte-for-byte, it can contain credentials already present in your files; do not share it. To recover, use npx pantheon-opencode restore [--project] [--yes]. A failure or interruption before the first managed write leaves configuration unchanged; after a write, the run is recorded as partial/applied and the backup is preserved. Recovery is manual through restore, not an automatic rollback.

docs.title: Removal and purge
docs.text:
The uninstaller can also be reviewed before applying:

npx pantheon-opencode uninstall --project --dry-run
npx pantheon-opencode uninstall --project --force

Without --force, applying asks for confirmation on a TTY and fails closed in a non-interactive environment. The uninstaller removes only items identified as Pantheon's, preserves symlinks, and backs up regular files it will change or remove; backups are not deleted by uninstall. On global installs it also undoes the native Context negation in cli.json, removing only the -opencode.sidebar.context directive (and the whole file when Pantheon created it), so the native Context block returns. --purge-data is narrower: it only allows removing .pantheon/install-state.json when it is a regular file and a verifiable schema-v2 state. It is not a general cleanup of .pantheon and does not remove backups. Review with --dry-run first; to apply purge non-interactively, combine --purge-data --force.

docs.title: Review drift in installed files
docs.text:
New installs keep a versioned per-file inventory for regular managed files (exact relative path, component/layout, hash, and mode; no content is stored). Use reconcile to identify files that have left the current source and remain identical to the installer's last write:

# Read-only preview; select --global or --target PATH when appropriate
npx pantheon-opencode reconcile --project --dry-run
npx pantheon-opencode reconcile --project --dry-run --components agents,skills
npx pantheon-opencode reconcile --global --target /caminho/config-opencode --dry-run
npx pantheon-opencode reconcile --target /caminho/projeto --dry-run

# Reviewable plan, applied in a separate invocation with explicit authorization
npx pantheon-opencode reconcile --project --components agents --save-plan .pantheon-reconcile.json
npx pantheon-opencode reconcile --apply-plan .pantheon-reconcile.json --yes

# Alternative: review and apply in the same invocation
npx pantheon-opencode reconcile --project --apply --yes

The preview writes or removes nothing. Apply revalidates the inventory, hashes, and exact operation set; any drift cancels before removal. Before deleting, it creates a restorable backup under .pantheon/backups/; use pantheon-opencode restore to recover. Only exact regular files are removed — directories are never deleted recursively. Unselected components remain outside reconciliation.

Pre-2.0 states and installs older than the inventory migrate to an empty list: their existing files are unknown/ambiguous and are never inferred as Pantheon-owned or removed automatically. Changed, missing, symlinked, invalid-path, or incompatible-layout files are also preserved. doctor distinguishes previously managed files that were modified or disappeared; when the current payload is unavailable, it reports that only the recorded hash was checked. reconcile accepts --project, --global, or --target PATH; an explicit target uses the project layout by default. Combine --global --target PATH to indicate that an explicit global target uses the flat global layout. This choice is neither inferred nor reinterpreted from the path. Without a readable inventory, there is no automatic cleanup.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• OpenCode 2.x — Install OpenCode. OpenCode 2.0.22 is known broken (no ctx.permission.assert). An OpenCode 1.x host is refused before any write.
  • Node.js >=26.4.0 — for npx pantheon-opencode init and Node-based Pantheon tooling (engines.node = >=26.4.0). Node 22, Node 24, and Node 26.0–26.3 are unsupported.
  • The optional pantheon_cost backend separately needs node:sqlite (Node >=22.5); this capability threshold does not lower package support.
  • Official OpenCode 2.x — a supported host — has a Bun runtime path and a separate Node build pinned to 26.4.0; no Bun minimum is implied.
  • Python 3.11+ — for MCP servers (optional, used by npm run setup)
  • Git — for version detection in TUI sidebar

docs.title: Package and dependency contract
docs.text:
The TUI plugin is a root workspace. package.json declares "workspaces": ["src/plugins/tui"], and the root package-lock.json carries a link: true entry for node_modules/pantheon-tui resolving to src/plugins/tui. A single npm ci --ignore-scripts at the root installs the root project and the TUI subpackage; there is no second install step, and npm ci --prefix src/plugins/tui is no longer part of any workflow.

For a checkout validation:

npm ci --ignore-scripts

npm ci is the only accepted path: there is no fallback to npm install, and PANTHEON_ALLOW_NPM_INSTALL_FALLBACK is not a supported escape hatch. The post-install TUI sync likewise propagates a failing npm ci; it does not silently repair or rewrite a lockfile.

docs.title: The nested TUI lockfile is still shipped, and still load-bearing
docs.text:
Two lockfiles exist and both are committed, but they now serve different consumers, which is worth being explicit about:

  • root package-lock.json — what the workspace install and CI use.
  • src/plugins/tui/package-lock.json — a published artifact. It is copied by scripts/sync-tui.mjs into the user's live plugin dir, where npm ci --omit=dev runs against it, not the root one. A manifest/lock divergence there makes every end user's npm install pantheon-opencode hard-fail inside postinstall.

That second lock can no longer be regenerated in place: under a workspaces parent, npm install --package-lock-only in the member directory reports "up to date" and folds the change into the root lock instead, and neither --workspaces=false nor --ignore-workspace-root-check changes that. Hand applying the same version to both files is valid only for a version change on a dependency already present in the lock's tree; adding or removing one requires generating the lock in an isolated directory (no workspace parent) and copying it back — and that regeneration re-resolves the entire transitive tree, so its diff must be reviewed. tests/tui-workspace-lock.test.mjs is the gate that catches a drift in either direction.

docs.title: Why overrides: { "rolldown": "1.2.7" } exists
docs.text:
tsdown@0.23.0 requires rolldown: "~1.2.7". The exact 1.2.7 override satisfies that range and keeps the workspace and standalone TUI installs on the same bundler, whose minifier output is part of the committed bundle. Pinning tsdown alone does not pin its dependency; a direct devDependency would not hold either because Node resolution can prefer a nearer nested copy. The root and standalone TUI overrides both enforce the same version. tsdown 0.23.0's engine range (^22.18.0 || ^24.11.0 || >=26.0.0) includes the project's declared Node support floor (>=26.4.0).

Two consequences a maintainer must know before touching it:

  • overrides bypasses range validation rather than erroring, so it can silently contradict a dependent's declared range. tests/tui-workspace-lock.test.mjs asserts the override against tsdown's declared range and that the root lock resolves exactly one rolldown; CI additionally asserts the installed version is exactly 1.2.7.
  • Changing it can alter minifier output and break the TUI dist freshness gate. Update both overrides, regenerate both locks, rebuild dist, and review the generated diff together.

docs.title: TUI production security overrides
docs.text:
The root and standalone TUI manifests override @babel/core to 7.29.7 (security floor >=7.29.6) and seroval to 1.6.8 (security floor >=1.6.3). The affected packages are reachable from the shipped TUI runtime; these pins clear the audited production advisories while upstream @opentui/solid@0.5.10 still pins Babel 7.28.0 and Solid 1.9.12.

seroval@1.6.8 is outside Solid 1.9.12's declared ~1.5.0 range. Keep solid-js pinned to the exact 1.9.12 peer required by OpenTUI rather than allowing a workspace copy of 1.9.15; tests/tui-workspace-lock.test.mjs checks both lock trees and exercises the Seroval serializer API used by Solid's server renderer. Run that regression, both clean install paths, and the production audit before changing these overrides. Remove them only when upstream dependency ranges accept patched releases and the production audit remains clear without them.

docs.title: Coverage reporting
docs.text:
npm run coverage runs test:node under Node's built-in --experimental-test-coverage and prints line/branch/function coverage for the .mjs/.js modules under scripts/, src/ and bin/. It adds no dependencies and enforces no threshold — the repository has no established coverage floor, so a percentage gate would fail immediately on pre-existing untested code and block unrelated work. The number is a baseline to improve against, not a gate.

What it does not cover: test:ts is a hand-rolled tsx loop with no node --test runner, so the 106 TypeScript files under src/ and bin/ are entirely unmeasured by this command; test:ci is pytest and reports no JavaScript coverage at all. Python coverage additionally requires pytest-cov, which is not declared in any requirements file — see src/mcp/requirements-mcp.txt.

docs.title: The plugin contract
docs.text:
Pantheon registers one plugin. The installer writes the <installed>/src/plugin directory under the plural plugins key, in the object form the host needs to deliver options:

{ "plugins": [{ "package": "<installed>/src/plugin", "options": {} }] }

The host gate must CONFIRM the host is OpenCode 2.x before any write: OPENCODE_VERSION=v2 pins the answer, an OPENCODE_BIN basename of opencode2 is an explicit operator hint, and otherwise a --version probe decides. A confirmed 1.x host, a failed probe, or an unreadable version is a hard refusal before any write — there is no fallback and no --opencode-version flag. The resolution order is documented once in Compatibility. The exact tool list is in Architecture; user-facing behavior is in OpenCode 2.x.

The installer strips Pantheon references from the legacy singular plugin key (a pre-2.0 config is recognized and migrated, never recreated) before writing the current registration, so a host never loads two Pantheon plugins. Third-party entries are retained and not converted.

docs.title: Config fields
docs.text: The installer writes native fields: providers, permissions, and MCP entries under mcp. The enforceable MCP rule is { "action": "<server>_*", "resource": "*", "effect": "deny" } (or the exact tool name). action: "mcp" and the legacy key permission.mcp.<server> are not evaluated by the host; the installer converts allow/deny and emits no rule for ask, because ask hides the tool instead of prompting.

docs.title: Jev decision model (optional)
docs.text:
The Zeus-only pantheon_jev_decide advisory tool registers automatically on hosts that expose the native Decisions API; using it requires the user-level decision-route configuration. Two ways:

# One command at install time (explicit caps required — no defaults):
npx pantheon-opencode init --decision-model opencode-console-jev/jev-1.13 \
  --decision-monthly-usd 5 --decision-per-decision-usd 0.10

# Or any time later:
npx pantheon-opencode decision-router setup-model opencode-console-jev/jev-1.13 \
  --monthly-usd 5 --per-decision-usd 0.10
npx pantheon-opencode decision-router doctor   # read-only route diagnosis

--decision-no-consent configures everything except egress consent. Other providers (TypeSafe direct, OpenRouter-hosted) and the full gate chain: Native Decisions. Performance tuning (hook costs, prompt budget, model tiers): Performance.

docs.title: Model overrides (pantheon_model)
docs.text:
There is no install-time model wizard. init accepts --model and --small-model for an explicit top-level override in the generated config (validating provider/model-id); --preset is refused — the legacy active-preset marker is not read by the installer.

Per-agent overrides belong to the pantheon_model tool. Both the tool and the /pantheon-model command write overrides to active-preset.json and never write .env or top-level model/small_model.

/pantheon-model status
/pantheon-model set --agent hermes --model opencode-go/gpt-5.6-terra --effort medium --scope project
/pantheon-model reset --agent hermes --scope project

The tool exposes explicit status, show, set, and reset actions and no wizard: project-only, rejecting scope=global and authorization flags in the same call. The /pantheon-model command with no arguments runs a legacy interactive wizard that still accepts global scope with separate confirm + authorize-global. Validation errors name the accepted agents, require provider/model-id, reject an unknown model or invalid effort (a valid effort above the model ceiling is clamped with a warning), and warn when a text-only model is requested for vision. Without an override the host model stays intact; delegates inherit the parent chat model natively. See MCP Tools.

docs.title: Optional vision step
docs.text: An interactive TTY install offers an optional vision step after the component and target prompts: automatic discovery (default, writes nothing), pin a provider/model (merges visionModel into the global opencode-vision.json atomically with a .bak), or skip. Non-interactive flows never prompt and never write vision config. /pantheon-vision shows the resolved target and origin, and its picker applies visionModel with the same atomic merge. See MCP for model precedence and the degradation chain.

docs.title: Delegation
docs.text:
OpenCode 2.x documents subagent as the child-session tool. It is a host tool, not a Pantheon-specific API; availability, schema, background support, and completion observability depend on the active runtime. A foreground call waits for the result; with background: true, where the schema supports it, the call returns a sessionID and the parent is notified on completion. task() is host/API terminology, not a guaranteed root tool name.

The brief, return contracts, retry rule, and the caller/target matrix are in Architecture. The installer does not register a Pantheon delegation tool.

docs.title: TUI installation
docs.text:
The TUI is an optional component installed by npm run setup or an install that includes the plugins component. The installer discovers the local plugin's index.ts + tui.ts pair and registers the copied directory through the plugins entry. Without the plugins component, no entry is installed.

The installer also cancels the host's builtin Context block by appending -opencode.sidebar.context to the global ~/.config/opencode/cli.json plugins array. The negation is global-only: a project install neither creates nor edits cli.json, so the native Context block can appear duplicated. uninstall removes exactly that directive (and the file when Pantheon created it). A cli.json that is not valid JSON, or whose plugins is not an array, is never overwritten; the install warns and continues.

The sidebar block and /dispatch panel are documented in OpenCode 2.x.

docs.title: TUI dev build
docs.text:
npm ci --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund
npm run build --prefix src/plugins/tui

Install the built plugin into .opencode/plugins/pantheon-tui so the directory contains the index.ts and tui.ts entrypoints. TUI plugins load at process start, so restart OpenCode after each build. Never add src/plugins/tui to opencode.json; that file is packaged and merged into user configs.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
Type these in the OpenCode chat:

Command Description /pantheon Multi-perspective council synthesis via inline agents /pantheon-audit 3-layer code audit: heuristic scan → Themis deep review → OWASP Top 10 /pantheon-deepwork Heavy multi-phase task with persisted checkpoints and Themis review gates /pantheon-model actions; pantheon_model tool (status\|show\|set\|reset) Manual per-agent overrides in active-preset.json (overrides.agents[agent]). The tool: explicit actions without a preset wizard, project-only; status shows project overrides and warnings; set takes agent, model, optional effort, and optionally scope: project; reset takes agent and optionally scope: project. Global files are neither read nor applied by the tool; the no-argument command runs a legacy wizard that still accepts global scope with separate confirm + authorize-global. Atomic write .bak+lock; never writes .env or top-level model. /pantheon-optimize Project optimization: bloat scan, deepwork archive, cache migration, token report /pantheon-consolidate Merge and deduplicate memory entries through the persistence MCP server

docs.title: Troubleshooting — keys and legacy presets
docs.text:
Static presets are retired from the runtime: PANTHEON_MODEL_PRESET and preset markers do not activate models. Only explicit project per-agent overrides are applied, global files are ignored by the tool, and without an override the host model stays intact. The set-tier CLI still activates a preset profile for provider configuration; the runtime ignores the marker.

No hardcoded secrets — only env var names + baseURLs below.

docs.title: Quick diagnosis
docs.text:
# see whether a legacy marker is present (it is ignored at runtime)
echo $PANTHEON_MODEL_PRESET
cat .pantheon/active-preset.json 2>/dev/null || cat ~/.config/opencode/.pantheon/active-preset.json 2>/dev/null || echo "nenhum active-preset.json (herança nativa)"

# per-agent status (no secrets)
/pantheon-model status
# or
/pantheon-model show

# validate preset defs
node scripts/validate-routing.mjs
# or
node -e "import('./src/pantheon/presets.mjs').then(m=>console.log(m.validatePresetDefs(m.loadPresetDefs())))"

docs.title: Headless / CI (no TTY)
docs.text: A non-interactive apply requires --yes. Without a TTY, init prints the plan and changes nothing unless --yes (alias -y) explicitly authorizes it. TTY defaults and headless defaults match; runtime and prompts are opt-in. Exit codes: 0 ok/plan-only/refused restore · 2 apply requested without authorization · 3 drift · 130 canceled · 1 failure.

docs.title: Backup, restore, and approval flow
docs.text:
• Preview: init --dry-run prints the plan and does not write to the target. For review across invocations, use --save-plan <file>; to apply the reviewed artifact, use --apply-plan <file> --yes (or confirm on the TTY). The versioned plan is written with mode 0600, includes metadata/fingerprints, and does not include generated content. It is bound to the original path, target, and package; apply recomputes operations and snapshots and aborts with code 3 on drift. Saved plans with --force/--clean are not accepted.
  • The host gate in the preview: a dry run runs the same gate as the apply, including the --version probe, which runs in a throwaway HOME/XDG sandbox with a 2-second timeout. A host the gate cannot confirm as 2.x refuses the preview like the apply; pass OPENCODE_VERSION=v2 to make the answer deterministic when no host binary can be probed.
  • Preview limits: the plan represents managed-file operations and names runtime effects when selected (venv create/reuse/recreate and dependency installation/download); it does not enumerate every installed dependency. Per-file detail is shown only with --verbose (or structured --json). postinstall/sync-tui is outside the approval flow. It is not a transaction and does not guarantee automatic rollback.
  • Exact backup: before the first write, init saves an exact set under .pantheon/backups/<timestamp>/ (directory 0700, files and manifest 0600; keeps the 5 most recent). It is a byte-for-byte copy and therefore also contains any API keys/tokens already present in your files — so it is never printed (nor are its hashes).
  • Restore: pantheon-opencode restore [--project] [--from <dir>] [--dry-run] [--yes]. It verifies the manifest integrity and refuses to restore a tampered set; it backs up the current state before reverting. In a non-interactive run it requires --yes; missing authorization fails closed without a backup or mutation. On a TTY it asks (default no): explicit decline exits 0, cancellation exits 130, and both leave files and backups unchanged.
  • Failure mid-apply: it aborts the remaining writes, cleans temporary files (<file>.tmp-<pid>), lists the paths already applied (without content), and prints the recovery instruction. There is no automatic rollback — the exact backup + restore is the recovery path (an interrupted apply is recoverable the same way).
  • Outside the approval flow: postinstall/sync-tui only resynchronizes TUI artifacts; it does not prompt or pass through the --yes gate.
# Headless apply with the default components
npx pantheon-opencode init --headless --yes

# No Python/MCP runtime
npx pantheon-opencode init --headless --yes --no-mcp

# Project-scoped install
npx pantheon-opencode init --headless --yes --project

# Decision-model activation in the same pass (explicit caps required)
npx pantheon-opencode init --headless --yes \
  --decision-model opencode-console-jev/jev-1.13 \
  --decision-monthly-usd 5 --decision-per-decision-usd 0.10

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
After installation, verify everything works:

# 1. Check agents are installed
ls ~/.config/opencode/agents/
# Should show 14 .md files

# 2. Check MCP servers
ls ~/.config/opencode/scripts/

# 3. Launch normally; use the conditional setting below only when supported.
opencode

# 4. Test delegation with the actual tool schema shown to Zeus
# In the reported Beta 10 runtime, dispatch through `subagent`; request
# background only if the active schema offers it.

# 5. Run health check
npm run doctor

If (and only if) the active host version/runtime documents and requires the experimental background setting, export OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_BACKGROUND_SUBAGENTS=true before launching OpenCode. Verify delegation against the tools actually exposed to Zeus; do not infer completion tracking or recovery from a successful dispatch.

Isolated global install: to test the installed package in an isolated sandbox (without contaminating the dev environment, which mixes several installs), use ~/pantheon-sandbox/ — run bash ~/pantheon-sandbox/run-test.sh (mcp list 5/5 + doctor + isolated TUI). This gate covers the prepared sandbox; it is not a support claim for every real host. The runner installs the current stable @opencode/cli by default; OPENCODE_V2_SPEC lets you select another build. Discard with rm -rf ~/pantheon-sandbox; details in ~/pantheon-sandbox/README.md.

docs.title: TUI runtime versus development build
docs.text:
The installer treats src/plugins/tui as the single source of truth and always copies it into the target config as plugins/pantheon-tui (the bundled dist/ + package.json). OpenCode's TUI loader reads the copied package.json exports map (./tui → dist/tui.js, ./server → dist/server.js), so users do not need tsconfig.json, tsdown, or development dependencies after installation. The TUI build and typecheck scripts are maintainer/development tasks for the repository, not post-install health checks; their failure in ~/.config/opencode/plugins/pantheon-tui does not indicate a broken runtime.

Every install (global or project) registers exactly ONE Pantheon TUI reference system-wide — the copied plugins/pantheon-tui directory in the installed config. Stale references from older installs (dist file paths, in-package src/plugins/tui dirs, bare plugins/pantheon-tui copies, npx paths) are removed from all tui.json locations OpenCode reads: ~/.opencode/tui.json, ~/.config/opencode/tui.json and <project>/.opencode/tui.json.

Windows/WSL: each environment (Windows native vs. WSL/Linux) uses its own OpenCode binary, config directory, and Node/npx install. Run the installer separately inside each environment — never share a config dir or copy tui.json references between them, since paths are environment-specific.

Problem Solution Agents not found Run npx pantheon-opencode init again MCP servers not starting Check Python 3.11+, run npm run setup Background delegation not available Check the active host version/runtime's tool schema and documentation. Set OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_BACKGROUND_SUBAGENTS=true only if that version documents support and requires it; the setting does not guarantee status, completion tracking, or recovery tools. TUI sidebar not showing Check the installed config's tui.json has exactly one plugins/pantheon-tui entry (absolute path) Plugin not loading Ensure <config>/plugins/pantheon-tui/dist/tui.js exists (copied at install time) Health check fails Run npm run doctor for detailed diagnostics

docs.title: MCP troubleshooting
docs.text: MCP startup and packaging failures are separate from TUI loading.

docs.title: Memory MCP packaging
docs.text: src/mcp/memory_mcp.py is the canonical Memory MCP server. The source-tree scripts/memory_mcp.py entrypoint delegates to it, and the runtime installer copies the canonical source into the installed scripts directory. install-mcp.mjs first resolves that installed copy and falls back to the source-tree entrypoint when running from a checkout. The script-sync test checks that both entrypoints expose the same tool list.

docs.title: MCP servers and spawn failure (ENOENT)
docs.text:
Pantheon's MCP servers (resources, code-mode, memory, persistence, vision) are spawned by OpenCode as local child processes. Two facts shape how spawn failures behave:

  1. OpenCode 1.18 does not retry a failed local MCP server. If the spawn fails at startup, the server stays in failed state for the whole TUI process. There is no reconnect hook; the only recovery is restarting the TUI. Session data and persistence are safe — they live in the SQLite database, not in the MCP process.
  2. posix_spawn ENOENT means the command path does not exist. The most common cause is a stale hardcoded path (e.g. a config that still points at /home/admin/.config/opencode/... after the home directory was migrated) or a path relative to an ambiguous root. OpenCode spawns the command verbatim — a missing interpreter or script fails with ENOENT before any Python code runs.

Diagnosis

# Verify the interpreter and script exist for each configured server
ls /home/ils15/.config/opencode/.venv/bin/python3
ls /home/ils15/.config/opencode/scripts/mcp_resources.py
# etc. — compare against the paths in ~/.config/opencode/opencode.json

# Static check — `npm run doctor` (or `pantheon-opencode doctor`) validates
# that every local MCP command's executable and absolute script args exist
npm run doctor -- --target /home/ils15/.config/opencode

If the doctor reports MCP "..." executable does not exist, fix the path in ~/.config/opencode/opencode.json (or re-run the installer, which resolves hermetic absolute paths — see below) and restart the OpenCode TUI.

Recovery

# Close the TUI (Ctrl+C / exit) and relaunch. Sessions and data persist.
opencode
# Verify MCP servers are back:
opencode mcp list

Hermetic path policy (P2, 2026-08-05)

  • scripts/install-mcp.mjs generates commands with absolute interpreter and script paths, resolved in this order: canonical user install (~/.config/opencode/.venv/bin/python3 + ~/.config/opencode/scripts/*.py), then the local checkout (<ROOT>/.venv + <ROOT>/scripts|src/mcp), with a warning fallback to PATH python3.
  • scripts/doctor.mjs now includes a hermetic spawn check: every local MCP entry is verified for an existing executable and existing absolute script args, so the ENOENT class is caught statically before OpenCode tries to spawn.
  • Avoid editing MCP commands to relative paths or paths under another user's home — they reproduce this failure class.

docs.title: Host/API task() Delegation Concept
docs.text:
This is an API-level illustration for hosts that expose the documented native task() shape and completion semantics. It is not a guarantee that Zeus has a root task() tool, that this signature is available, or that dispatch returns a trackable result. In the reported Beta 10 Zeus-root runtime, dispatch was via subagent; task_status and cancel_task were not exposed, and no status, completion-tracking, or recovery guarantee follows from this diagram. Check the active runtime's tool schema and documentation. Background support, the experimental environment variable, and completion notifications are version/runtime-dependent.

sequenceDiagram
    participant Z as Zeus
    participant A as Apollo (child)
    participant H as OpenCode host

    Z->>H: host API dispatch (e.g. task(), if exposed)
    H-->>A: child session starts (host-dependent)
    A-->>H: child completion (if emitted by host)
    opt Host exposes a result or completion notification
        H-->>Z: host-defined result/notification
    end

    Note over Z,H: Illustrative host API only; no Pantheon-specific delegate API

docs.title: MCP Servers
docs.text:
🇧🇷 Versão em Português disponível: Leia em Português

Pantheon ships five local Python stdio MCP servers. They auto-start with OpenCode and cover project memory, persistence, resources, confined script execution, and vision. This page owns MCP setup, entrypoints, allowlists, and pins. Tool signatures live in MCP Tools; memory policy lives in Memory.

flowchart LR
    Host["💻 OpenCode 2.x Host Engine"]

    subgraph MCP_Venv["🐍 Isolated Python venv (FastMCP 4.1.2 & MCP 2.2.0)"]

        Code["⚡ pantheon-code-mode<br/>(Confined scripts & approvals)"]
        Mem["🧠 pantheon-memory<br/>(SQLite FTS5 durable facts)"]
        Pers["💾 pantheon-persistence<br/>(Session checkpoints & goals)"]
        Vis["👁️ pantheon-vision<br/>(Local image inspection)"]
    end

    Host <-->|"stdio (JSON-RPC)"| Code
    Host <-->|"stdio (JSON-RPC)"| Mem
    Host <-->|"stdio (JSON-RPC)"| Pers

    Mem <--> DB1[("memory.db")]
    Pers <--> DB2[("persistence.db")]

docs.title: Runtime pins
docs.text: The packaged runtime pins the MCP Python SDK to mcp==2.2.0 and the standalone FastMCP server framework to fastmcp==4.1.2. Server code imports FastMCP from fastmcp; MCP SDK v2 removed the old mcp.server.fastmcp re-export. Installation creates the isolated Python environment from the matching manifest in src/mcp/.

docs.title: Entrypoints
docs.text:
The installer declares the five servers in scripts/install-mcp.mjs:74-78 and registers them at :196-301. Each entrypoint is a real script, not a shared server.py:

Server Entrypoint Tools Resources pantheon-resources scripts/mcp_resources.py — 4 static + 6 templates pantheon-code-mode scripts/code_mode.py 2 1 static + 1 template pantheon-memory scripts/memory_mcp.py 9 — pantheon-persistence scripts/mcp_persistence.py 6 — pantheon-vision src/mcp/pantheon_vision.py 3 —

The entrypoints were renamed away from the shared *_server.py token. The installer heals stale paths with the mapping in scripts/install/config-migration.mjs:700-706:

Old New mcp_resources_server.py mcp_resources.py code_mode_server.py code_mode.py memory_mcp_server.py memory_mcp.py mcp_persistence_server.py mcp_persistence.py pantheon_vision_server.py pantheon_vision.py

Installation writes absolute paths for the venv interpreter and the server script. pantheon-memory uses src/mcp/memory_mcp.py as its canonical runtime source; scripts/memory_mcp.py is a source-tree compatibility entrypoint that delegates to it. pantheon-vision is deployed from the canonical source to scripts/pantheon_vision.py; do not maintain a second source copy.

docs.title: OpenCode configuration
docs.text:
The installer writes this shape. Add the same shape by hand only for a custom server.

{
  "mcp": {
    "pantheon-resources": {
      "type": "local",
      "command": ["<venv-python>", "<installed>/scripts/mcp_resources.py"],
      "enabled": true
    },
    "pantheon-code-mode": {
      "type": "local",
      "command": ["<venv-python>", "<installed>/scripts/code_mode.py"],
      "cwd": ".",
      "enabled": true
    }
  }
}

Restart the client after changing MCP configuration. Servers are separate OS processes launched by the host.

docs.title: Per-agent allowlists
docs.text:
The installer reads mcp_tools from each canonical src/agents/*.md file and generates native per-agent permissions. For each Pantheon server it denies the wildcard first, then allows the declared tools. Undeclared Pantheon servers default to deny; unrelated user MCP servers are untouched.

Agent Resources Code-mode Memory Persistence Vision zeus all — search context_save, context_get, goal_create, goal_get, goal_update, goal_done — athena all — search, code_query, code_neighbors — — apollo all — search, code_query, code_neighbors — — hermes all execute script search — — aphrodite all execute script search — describe/OCR/analyze demeter all execute script search — — themis all execute script search — — prometheus all execute script search — — hephaestus all execute script search — — nyx all execute script search — — gaia all — recall — describe/OCR/analyze iris all — recall — — mnemosyne all execute script explicit memory tools — — talos all execute script recall — —

Rules:

  • all allows every tool from that named Pantheon server.
  • A list allows only those tool names; an empty list denies every tool there.
  • A server omitted from an agent's metadata is denied for that agent.
  • Rules are generated into V1 permission objects and V2 permissions arrays.
  • V1 permission.task rules translate to V2's native subagent action.
  • Third-party MCP permissions remain the user's configuration.

On OpenCode 2.x the host evaluates a permissions rule whose action is <server>_* (or <server>_<tool>) with effect deny/allow. The V1-shaped permission.mcp.<server> key is not an action the host evaluates; the installer translates allow/deny into the former. ask is not expressible for MCP on that host: it hides the tool instead of prompting, so the installer emits no rule and warns. In V2, per-agent rules can hide tools from that agent without disconnecting the server.

The Apollo/Athena code_query and code_neighbors grants are the approved read-only code-map choice; code_index and per-project binding were not selected. Checkpoints are limited to context_save and context_get on Zeus; they are session-qualified temporary persistence, not durable memory writes. Mnemosyne's canonical allowlist includes durable-memory write tools; always check the active tool list. These are installed per-agent allowlists, not a guarantee that the root runtime exposes the same tools.

docs.title: pantheon-resources
docs.text:
Read-only resource server exposing Pantheon framework metadata. No tools, only resources and templates.

URI Description pantheon://routing Canonical delegation rules and handoff contracts pantheon://agents All 14 agents with roles from frontmatter pantheon://skills All skills with descriptions pantheon://eval Latest certification scores from the plugin_eval namespace pantheon://agents/{agent_name} One agent file by name (case-insensitive) pantheon://deepwork/{slug} PLAN.md for a deepwork task pantheon://deepwork/{slug}/status STATUS.md for a deepwork task pantheon://memory-bank/{path} One file under .pantheon/memory-bank/ (path traversal blocked) pantheon://skills/{name} One skill's SKILL.md pantheon://eval/{plugin} One certification report

pantheon://memory-bank/{path} reads project documentation on demand; those files are not automatically loaded. The evaluation resources read the global Memory SQLite database in the plugin_eval namespace, which is an organizational filter, not an access-control boundary.

docs.title: pantheon-code-mode
docs.text:
Confined script execution from .pantheon/code-mode/, with a 30-second timeout. It exposes two tools: execute_code_script(script_name) runs an approved script, and approve_code_script(script_name) records or refreshes its SHA-256 in the manifest. Resources list the available scripts and show one script's content.

Scripts run only when explicitly approved and recorded in the manifest with their SHA-256. See Code Mode for the approval contract and status codes.

docs.title: pantheon-memory
docs.text:
Persistent SQLite memory with FTS5/BM25 lexical search. It registers six memory_* tools plus three code_* codemap tools; the canonical source is src/mcp/memory_mcp.py. The database defaults to ~/.config/opencode/memory/memory.db, with PANTHEON_HOME and XDG_CONFIG_HOME overrides.

Tool signatures are in MCP Tools; the size cap, TTL, search policy, and error contract are in Memory.

docs.title: pantheon-persistence
docs.text:
Session checkpoints plus manual session goals. The surface is exactly six tools: context_save, context_get, goal_create, goal_get, goal_update, and goal_done. The KV table is internal checkpoint storage; former KV management, context list/statistics, rehydration, and summary operations are not registered.

Goals are Zeus-only and partitioned by OpenCode session id; the session id is a correlation key, not authentication. See Memory for permissions, TTL defaults, size bounds, and migration of an existing database.

docs.title: pantheon-vision
docs.text:
Three tools: vision_describe(path, prompt?, session_id?), vision_ocr(path, session_id?), and vision_analyze(path, session_id?).
