Read the caller session's active or latest completed goal Zeus goal_update (goal_id, expected_version, title?, description?, clear_description?) Edit goal fields with optimistic version checking Zeus goal_done (goal_id, expected_version) Complete the caller session's goal Zeus

Goal tools are Zeus-only because goals are session-scoped and cannot be read across sessions. Athena and Themis run in child sessions and cannot read Zeus's goal; as root they cannot create a goal in their own session because only Zeus has goal_create. Manual goals do not enable automatic continuation and do not replace the V1 GoalStore. See Memory for details.

docs.title: pantheon-code-mode (script execution)
docs.text:
Confined automation scripts from .pantheon/code-mode/. Two tools, 30s default timeout (override per script via YAML frontmatter timeout), .sh and .py only.

The server also registers pantheon://code-mode/scripts and pantheon://code-mode/scripts/{name} resources; these are not part of pantheon-resources.

Tool Signature Description Who uses it execute_code_script (script_name: str, args?: list[str], json_output?: bool) Run an approved script from .pantheon/code-mode/. Returns a plain-text summary, or with json_output=true a structured dict with stdout, stderr, exit_code, duration_ms, timed_out and frontmatter metadata Agents that grant pantheon-code-mode: [execute_code_script] approve_code_script (script_name: str, json_output?: bool) Record or refresh the script's SHA-256 in the approval manifest. Execution is opt-in: only approved scripts whose hash matches run No bundled agent — see Unreachable by any agent

Agents granted: aphrodite, demeter, hephaestus, hermes, mnemosyne, nyx, prometheus, talos

Agents without a grant: apollo, athena, gaia, iris, themis, zeus

These are exact mcp_tools.pantheon-code-mode frontmatter grants, not a bash permission: mnemosyne holds the grant while declaring bash: deny, and iris allows only the scoped commands git * and gh *. Zeus has no code-mode grant; its prompt records that execute_code_script was removed and that execution is delegated.

Use cases by agent (illustrative, not exhaustive): | Agent | Typical scripts | |-------|----------------| | hermes | pytest, ruff check, ruff format | | aphrodite | Focused tests for the changed surface; full npm test only when the scope or risk warrants it; biome check | | demeter | alembic upgrade head && pytest | | prometheus | Docker builds, CI/CD pipeline scripts | | talos | Automated hotfix sequences, batch fixes |

Call pattern: 

execute_code_script("lint-and-test.sh", args=["backend/"])

docs.title: pantheon-vision (image analysis)
docs.text:
The local vision server accepts local paths, file: URIs, data URIs, and HTTP(S) image URLs. The plugin first tries its configured native gateway, then falls back to this MCP. Bifrost is not a default dependency; use it only through an explicit PANTHEON_VISION_TOOL or imageAnalysisTool setting.

Tool Signature Description vision_describe (path: str, prompt?: str, session_id?: str) Describe image content, visible text, layout, and objects vision_ocr (path: str, session_id?: str) Extract visible text while preserving line formatting vision_analyze (path: str, session_id?: str) Return image metadata, description, and OCR as JSON

Permission: ask is recommended because images or remote URLs are sent to the configured gateway. The server reads PANTHEON_OPENCODE_API_KEY or OPENCODE_API_KEY, then the OpenCode auth store; no API key is stored in the repository configuration.

docs.title: OpenCode plugin tools
docs.text:
These tools are provided by the OpenCode plugin, not by one of the five native MCP servers listed above.

Tool Arguments What it reports pantheon_model action?: status\|show\|set\|reset, plus action-specific agent/model/effort and optional scope: project V2 manual overrides are project-only: status reads project configuration, and the agent transform applies only explicit project per-agent model/variant overrides; global files are neither read nor applied. set/reset reject scope: global and any confirm/authorize_global fields before writing. Global overrides require separate explicit human authorization in a future surface and are not supported by this tool; flags in the same tool call are not approval. V2 ignores static preset markers and PANTHEON_MODEL_PRESET, leaving host defaults intact otherwise. Invalid or malformed project overrides preserve the host model and expose warnings via status. The V2 server plugin has no documented toast or other proactive user-visible notification API during transform, so no toast/proactive warning is promised. V1 behavior remains legacy. pantheon_cost days?: 1..365 (default 7), session?: <root session id>, refreshPricing?: boolean Read-only token totals and USD cost by agent and phase, by model, and by session, in a rolling days × 24-hour window from query time. It is not a calendar-day or session window. pantheon_local_decision schemaVersion: 1, structured candidate agent/skill/resource IDs, domain?, gateStatus, bounded complexity dimensions Zeus-only (identity from the host tool context) local advisory selector over the caller-supplied candidates. Deterministic, offline, fail-closed; never dispatches, searches, or changes grants. Obvious work should skip it and go straight to native subagent. pantheon_jev_decide schemaVersion: 1, state: string (≤12k), questions: 1–4 typed (choice 2–16 options, score 2–10 levels, predicate) Zeus-only advisory typed decisions answered by the Jev decision model through the host's native Decisions API (no Pantheon transport). Registers only on hosts exposing that API; refuses without enabled config, egress consent, a cap-valid ledger candidate, or a host permission allow; settles the budget reservation from host-reported cost. Returns validated answers with confidence plus effect: 'none' — advice only.

Prices come from the public models.dev catalog (USD per 1M tokens: input, output, cache read and cache write), cached at <configDir>/cache/models-dev.json, where <configDir> follows the usual resolution — PANTHEON_HOME, else $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/opencode, else ~/.config/opencode. A tool call reads that cache and never waits on the network: a missing or older-than-24 h cache is refreshed in the background with a 3 s timeout and the report says the prices it used are stale. Only refreshPricing: true waits for that bounded refresh, and it is how new prices are forced. PANTHEON_COST_OFFLINE=1 forbids every network request on every path: the lazy background refresh is not scheduled, and refreshPricing: true is refused outright — the report then says Pricing: REFUSED, names this variable, and makes no request at all. An unknown or ambiguous model, or cache tokens with no published cache rate, read — and are excluded from the total, which then says (partial) — a model the catalog prices at zero stays $0.00, because an unknown model is never reported as free. Passing session scopes the whole report to that root session plus its descendant sessions, resolved through the parent_id links already in the database. Costs are catalog list prices, not a provider invoice; on V2 the phase can be unknown; and the node:sqlite CLI-fallback path still reports tokens only, with the report saying so.

docs.title: Cost backend and attribution
docs.text:
pantheon_cost prefers a read-only node:sqlite connection to the selected opencode.db (src/pantheon/cost-command.ts). When node:sqlite is unavailable in the host runtime — for example under Bun — the tool falls back to spawning node scripts/cost.mjs as a read-only subprocess. The fallback resolves a real Node binary, PANTHEON_NODE first and then node on PATH, verifies that it supports node:sqlite (Node >= 22.5), and runs the script with an argument array, never through a shell. If neither source resolves, the tool returns status: UNSUPPORTED. Database failures return a contract status such as UNAVAILABLE or CORRUPT_DATA and include diagnostic detail, including captured stderr when available.

Variable Default Purpose PANTHEON_NODE node from PATH Node >= 22.5 binary used only for the node:sqlite capability in the CLI fallback. An explicit path must exist and be executable, otherwise the tool fails fast PANTHEON_COST_OFFLINE unset Set to 1 to forbid every network request, including refreshPricing: true. The report uses the cached catalog only, an explicit refresh is refused with a Pricing: REFUSED notice naming this variable, and no socket is opened PANTHEON_COST_DB unset Absolute path to the database, checked before OPENCODE_DB OPENCODE_DB unset Absolute path to the database, checked before the XDG default

The database is resolved by path in this order: an explicit dbPath from the tool caller, PANTHEON_COST_DB, OPENCODE_DB, then the XDG default opencode.db. There is no per-version filename in that chain: opencode-v2.db is not a host 2.x database — it is a name a sandbox gives its own state database through OPENCODE_DB.

The v1/v2 distinction is the detected schema, not the file name. The report looks for the message and session_message tables and reads whichever the open database actually holds, because a migrated database carries both families at once. PANTHEON_OPENCODE_VERSION=v1|v2 selects no file: it only narrows an already-detected set to one table family, and fails fast when the value is invalid or the requested family is not there. A database carrying neither table returns CORRUPT_DATA; a ledger that exists but yields no readable tokens returns UNSUPPORTED, never a successful empty report.

The report always includes ## Cost by agent and adds ## Cost by model and ## Cost by session tables. A session row covers that session alone; passing session:<id> sums the root session and its descendants. An unpriced row reads — and is excluded from the total, which then says (partial).

docs.title: Naming in OpenCode
docs.text:
Pantheon runs only on OpenCode, which exposes an MCP tool as {server}_{tool} — for example pantheon-memory_memory_recall. The older multi-platform naming examples were removed with multi-platform support in v1.0.

In the Code Mode execute sandbox the visible catalog is a subset, not the registry above. Resolve a hidden tool by calling search() for its exact path and then invoking that path literally — passing the whole path string as a single key fails even though search() returned it.

docs.title: Measured usage baseline (2026-11-05 audit)
docs.text:
bench/mcp-usage-audit.mjs measures real native-MCP usage across four local, read-only sources (transcript session_message, the memory MCP database, the persistence kv databases, hooks.log bench lines) and writes a dated report to bench/results/. First measured run — 183k assistant messages, 8.7k user turns, 1.5k sessions with MCP activity:

Server Execute blocks Verdict from the data pantheon-memory 5,760 Over-firing on store (1,918 calls; most stored content was session narration — subtask summaries, delegation status, debugging play-by-play — not durable facts). Reads (search/recall ≈ 2,787) are the point and stay. pantheon-persistence 2,546 Checkpoints over-fire per turn (1,003 context_save → only 465 distinct checkpoints; the same key:"latest" re-saved turn after turn). kv rows are platform machinery (delegation telemetry), not model judgment. pantheon-vision 84 Legitimate (real screenshots only). Single waste pattern: three passes (describe + analyze + OCR) on one image. pantheon-code-mode 54 Barely used; keep as-is. pantheon-resources 47 Barely used; keep as-is.

Cost model (what "weigh the cost" means per server): pantheon-vision is real gateway spend per image call; pantheon-memory reads ride in the model's context for the rest of the session (per-token cost), and a bad store is a cost paid by every future session that recalls it; persistence checkpoints are near-free locally but add turn noise. The usage policies in zeus.md (durable-facts-only stores, milestone-only checkpoints, one vision pass per image) are the correction this baseline justifies.

Field finding — grants vs the execute bridge: mcp_tools grants gate which MCP tools a model may call directly. On the Code Mode execute path the model addresses servers programmatically regardless of grants — measured proof: zeus (granted memory_search only) made 1,918 memory_store calls. Grants are the matrix of intent and of the direct-call surface, not an enforcement wall; usage policy lives in the agent instructions.

Run the audit: node bench/mcp-usage-audit.mjs (adds --db, --stdout).

docs.title: Permission Tiers
docs.text:
OpenCode MCP tool grants authorize an agent to call the server tools exposed to it. They are not an OS-level sandbox and do not constrain the MCP process's permissions under the host user's OS account. The API/data boundary is therefore not limited to the repository: granted pantheon-memory tools operate on the user's global Memory database (~/.config/opencode/memory/memory.db by default; PANTHEON_HOME / XDG_CONFIG_HOME can override the root). code_query and code_neighbors read that global database's code index. Its code_files table has no project column, so results can include entities from any project previously indexed on this machine; these grants do not provide per-project isolation. No agent is granted code_index; its server-side path-confinement guard is defense in depth, not a project-isolation boundary for query results. Granted pantheon-persistence checkpoint tools can operate on the user's global database (~/.config/opencode/persistence/global.db by default) or the active project database (.pantheon/persistence/project.db), according to the scopes exposed by those tools. Manual goal tools use the Persistence deployment database and partition by session ID; a global install shares it across projects. Grants gate calls to registered MCP operations; they do not restrict the process's underlying OS permissions.

Server Recommended Tier Rationale pantheon-resources allow Read-only, same trust boundary as repo pantheon-code-mode ask Executes scripts — needs user confirmation pantheon-memory Per-agent exact mcp_tools lists above Host grants authorize only each listed tool; they are not an OS sandbox, and Memory data/index records use the user-global database pantheon-persistence per-agent exact tools Checkpoint tools can use the user-global or project database; manual goals are session-scoped in the deployment database, shared across projects in a global install pantheon-vision ask Sends image input to the configured vision gateway

docs.title: Security Notes
docs.text:
• pantheon-resources — path traversal protection on memory-bank/{path}
  • pantheon-code-mode — only .sh/.py in .pantheon/code-mode/, 30s timeout, no ../ escape
  • pantheon-memory — SQLite data in ~/.config/opencode/memory/memory.db by default (PANTHEON_HOME / XDG_CONFIG_HOME can override it); agent tool grants determine which tools are available
  • pantheon-persistence — checkpoint database at ~/.config/opencode/persistence/global.db by default; project scope uses .pantheon/persistence/project.db. PANTHEON_HOME / XDG_CONFIG_HOME override the global root.
  • pantheon-vision — 25 MB image cap, supported-format validation, safe errors, and API-key redaction

See skill: mcp-security for complete rules.

docs.title: Unreachable by any agent
docs.text:
These tools are registered by the runtime sources but no bundled agent grants them. This is intentional pending a future evidence-based grant; the list is verified against the MCP decorators and agent frontmatter by tests/agent-mcp-grants.test.mjs.

Server Exposed tools with no agent grant pantheon-code-mode approve_code_script pantheon-memory code_index

docs.title: OpenCode 2.x
docs.text: OpenCode 2 gets the Pantheon plugin: host-native tools, hooks, and a native TUI surface. This page covers what a user sees. The plugin contract, tool-by-tool registration, and the delegation matrix are in Architecture; supported hosts and evidence are in Compatibility.

docs.title: The host gate
docs.text: The installer must confirm the host is OpenCode 2.x before writing. There is no generation to select and no fallback: OPENCODE_VERSION=v2 pins the answer, an OPENCODE_BIN basename of opencode2 is an explicit operator hint, and otherwise a --version probe decides. A confirmed 1.x host, a failed probe, or an unreadable version is a hard refusal before any write. The resolution order and the exact refusal behavior live in Compatibility. One plugin is registered; a host never loads two Pantheon plugins.

docs.title: Tools
docs.text:
The plugin registers tools through ctx.tool.transform(). The exact list, with source locators, is in Architecture. In user terms:

  • hashline_edit edits files by line-tag anchors instead of raw line numbers.
  • pantheon_cost reports tokens and USD by agent, model, and session.
  • pantheon_model shows, sets, or resets per-agent project-scoped model overrides.
  • pantheon_local_decision is the advisory local decision selector; it runs only for Zeus.
  • vision_describe appears when the host exposes its model catalog.
  • pantheon_bounded_read appears when the host exposes its permission and session APIs, and only in a root Zeus session.

The three legacy goal tools are not registered. Use the Persistence MCP goal_* tools for durable manual goals; see Memory.

docs.title: Per-agent MCP permissions
docs.text:
The installer reads each agent's mcp_tools allowlist and generates native per-agent permissions. On OpenCode 2.x the host evaluates a permissions rule whose action is <server>_* (or <server>_<tool>) with effect deny/allow. The legacy permission.mcp.<server> key is not an action the host evaluates; the installer translates allow/deny into the former. ask is not expressible for MCP on that host — it hides the tool instead of prompting, so the installer emits no rule and warns.

An existing native permissions array remains authoritative. The installer does not append its legacy default grants to that array; it seeds those defaults only when the config has no native permissions array yet.

Deny-by-default, the entrypoints, and custom-server setup are in MCP.

docs.title: Dispatch sidebar block
docs.text:
The native sidebar shows the Pantheon version, active preset/source, git state, a Context block with thousands-separated tokens and <percent>% used of <window> (blue ≤25%, green ≤50%, yellow ≤90%, red above), $<spent> spent, and a muted cache <n>% · <n.n> tok/s line.

One aggregated Dispatch block covers the whole child set:

  • header ◈ Dispatch · <n> rodando · $<cost>, summing every child, live and finished;
  • one row per live child (⠸ <agent>·<kind> $<cost> <duration>, newest first, three then … +N rodando);
  • finished children rolled up per agent: ✓ <total> · $<sum> · <M> agentes (plus · <F> falhas when any child failed), up to three <agent> ×<count>·<kind> $<sum> rows and … +K $<sum> beyond — never one row per session.

The ·<kind> suffix says why the child exists: coun/plan/revw/hot/ disc from an explicit [council]/[plan]/[review]/[hotfix]/[discovery] prefix on the subagent description, otherwise from the agent (athena→plan, themis→revw, talos→hot, apollo→disc, anything else→oth). council is never inferred from an agent. A ~ after the kind marks a background child.

The block stays within eight lines and is omitted entirely when the session has no child. It is added with append claims: the native prompt footer keeps its own line, and Pantheon only appends ▸<preset> · ✦<n> ativos while delegations are running.

docs.title: /dispatch panel
docs.text:
/dispatch (also in the palette as Pantheon: Dispatch) opens pantheon.dispatch in the host's session.panel slot: a full-width view of the same delegation tree, rendered from the same collector as the sidebar block, so a child is never listed twice.

The header is ◈ Dispatch — <session> (+ [fullscreen]) with counters for the whole tree (2 rodando · 70 concluídos · 1 falha · $3.59; a zero counter is omitted) over one row per child — ⠋ prometheus plan $0.09 14m34s — running first, then most recent activity, with ✓/✗/○/? for completed/failed/interrupted/unknown. The detail pane shows the selected child's title or spawning description, short id, model, in/out/reasoning/cache tokens, kind evidence, and parent id; — means the host did not publish it.

Panels at least 72 columns put the detail beside the list; narrower ones stack it under the list and truncate per column. Keys are namespaced and bound (k/up, j/down, home, end, pageup, pagedown, enter, f, escape/q) and live inside the panel claim, so they stay inert while the panel is not focused. The list is paged at ten rows and selection is held by session id.

The panel reads only host-cached state — no session sync, no child message.list, no HTTP — and its 80 ms spinner tick exists only while the panel is open with something running. Opening it requires an open session; otherwise Pantheon toasts Open a session to view Dispatch instead of inventing a route. Jumping from a row to the child session is a documented TODO: no session router destination is verified for a child id.

docs.title: Plan before approval
docs.text:
When you ask for a plan or start /pantheon-deepwork, Athena returns the full plan to Zeus, who displays it in the main conversation before asking for approval. The approval prompt never points to a plan hidden in a child agent's conversation.

Zeus · teampro

  ## Plan: MCP permission audit

  1. Read every agent allowlist in src/agents/*.md
  2. Compare it with the `permissions` rules pantheon-init emits
  3. Report drift and update docs/MCP.md where a rule is undocumented
  4. Verify with npm run test:node and npm run docs:lint

  Files: docs/MCP.md, src/agents/*.md, scripts/install/*.mjs
  Risks: an `ask` rule cannot be expressed for MCP on this host

  Approve this plan? (yes / no)

Illustrative layout — not a screenshot. The plan is printed in the main conversation before the question, so approval never refers to a child's view.

OpenCode 2.x · pantheon-opencode 1.6.0

docs.title: Context pruning
docs.text:
The compaction hook performs dynamic context pruning on the provider-bound message array immediately before summarization, so old tool output is not re-summarized into permanent context.

  • It rewrites tool parts only.
  • An invocation repeated with the same tool name and normalized arguments keeps its most recent result verbatim; every earlier successful body becomes a [pantheon-prune:v1 …] placeholder.
  • Error results are never rewritten. A group is pruned only when its newest invocation carries a successful result.
  • Arguments of failed calls are blanked after two turns while the error text stays visible.
  • The last four turns and a protected tool list (subagent, task, skill) are never touched.
  • The marker makes a second pass a no-op, and a pass estimated below 200 tokens does nothing.

The hook log records savings for changed passes and the first occurrence of each fixed no-op reason (no-candidates or below-threshold) per session and hook site. These entries contain counts and estimated tokens only; tool content and arguments are not logged.

The array is mutated in place: no message is deleted or reordered, system is untouched, and an unexpected shape fails open without throwing. The same engine is available per request only when the plugin entry sets options.context_pruner.enabled to true (default false), because per-request pruning invalidates the provider prompt cache. keepTurns, purgeAfterTurns, protectedTools, minSavingsTokens, and charsPerToken tune it.

init writes the entry in its object form ({ "package": …, "options": { … } }), so there is a place to put that key without guessing the syntax — a bare-string entry leaves the host with no options at all. The context-pruner option and default are listed in the README's Plugin options table. Memory retrieval uses the pantheon-memory MCP only when an agent explicitly calls memory_search; see Memory.

docs.title: Session goals
docs.text: Durable manual goals are Persistence MCP tools, not plugin tools: goal_create, goal_get, goal_update, and goal_done. They are granted only to Zeus, partitioned by OpenCode session id, and never continue a session automatically. See Memory.

docs.title: Task-result guard
docs.text:
The execute.after chain runs task-result-guard → context-sandbox → read-enhancer. The guard intercepts native child-session dispatch where the child returns an empty or missing result. Instead of surfacing a silent completed with no payload, it raises an explicit error. This catches the common free-tier failure mode where a child exceeds the uncached-prefill token budget and returns nothing.

Background dispatch and status/fan-in facilities are runtime-dependent. When no status tool is visible, use synchronous subagent dispatch or wait for a host-provided completion notification; do not claim deterministic fan-in or job recovery without an exposed, verified mechanism.

docs.title: Unsupported features
docs.text:
The plugin reports these gaps through getUnsupportedFeatures() (the seed in src/pantheon/unsupported.mjs):

  • Adapter scope choices: legacy-hooks (the hook surface of the removed V1 plugin line), catalog-transform, integration-transform, skill-transform, goal-tools (the goal loop needs infrastructure the host's plugin context does not expose).
  • Host-domain gaps: idle-todo-enforcer (the enforcer is constructed only when the host's session domain exposes todo/messages/children/promptAsync; the measured 2.x domain does not), tool-ceiling (no message.updated producer for the host-reported budget, so the <tool_ceiling> block is not injected), todo-restore (no todo API to snapshot across compaction), and board-transitions (the shared board is reachable through the injected board, but the writers — terminal audit, idle reports, dispatch mirror — lived in the removed generation's event hook and pantheon-hooks.ts).

Everything else the removed generation wired is here: the Zeus read guard, the compaction context, vision history sanitization, the post-write formatter, and the delegation audit trail (start/stop records joined on delegation_id). Idle dispatch is wired but conditional — it reaches an enforcer only where idle-todo-enforcer is not in the seed, which is why that marker is listed above. pantheon_bounded_read applies the same code-root restriction as the read guard: src/, tests/ and scripts/ are refused; docs, config, the memory bank and .pantheon/ remain readable.

docs.title: Quota & usage
docs.text: The Pantheon TUI no longer ships a quota surface. The native quota panel, the sidebar quota block, usage history, and the pantheon.quota RPC were removed in 1.6.2; the sidebar keeps only the non-quota blocks (Pantheon version, preset/source, git state, Context, Todo, Dispatch).

docs.title: Recommended: the community plugin
docs.text:
To see provider quota and usage inside OpenCode, install the recommended community plugin:

opencode plugin add @slkiser/opencode-quota

This path requires OpenCode 2.0.26 or newer. On an OpenCode 1.x host, use the plugin's own installer instead:

npx @slkiser/opencode-quota@4 init

One line on coverage: @slkiser/opencode-quota supports 20+ providers and ships /quota, /quota_usage, and /quota_status terminal commands, a TUI surface, a Desktop app, and i18n — see github.com/slkiser/opencode-quota for the provider matrix and troubleshooting.

docs.title: What Pantheon still shows natively
docs.text:
• The sidebar Context block: tokens, percent gauge, $<spent> spent, and the muted cache <n>% · <n.n> tok/s line — all derived from the session transcript and the local OpenCode stats route, no provider calls.
  • The pantheon_cost tool: tokens and USD by agent, model, and session, read from the session database and priced with the models.dev catalog.

docs.title: Agent Reference — Pantheon
docs.text: This directory indexes the definitions for all 14 Pantheon agents. The canonical files live in src/agents/ and use the .md extension; their frontmatter specifies tools, model tier, capabilities, and delegation rules.

docs.title: Agents

docs.title: Domain artifacts and exclusivity (measured 2026-11-05)
docs.text:
Each specialist owns the durable artifact of its domain — the file the NEXT session reads first — and the exclusivity that pays is already enforced by grants, not by new tooling (the MCP usage audit found no delivery friction a new exclusive tool would remove; new exclusive tools fail the measured bar).

Agent Domain artifact (authors/maintains) Exclusive tooling verdict zeus AGENTS.md managed region, routing.yml Gate chain, budget ledger, persistence goal tools — grant-exclusive ✓ athena docs/plans/<slug>.md — the plan artifact a session executes against Plan-only contract is the exclusivity apollo none — read-only; delivers structured Briefs in-session Read-only contract is the exclusivity hermes docs/api/conventions.md — REST shapes, errors, auth, async patterns Shared execute_code_script; no new tool aphrodite docs/ui/conventions.md — tokens, layout, a11y, component patterns — kept current whenever the project has a graphical surface Vision grant trio (describe/ocr/analyze) — grant-exclusive ✓ demeter docs/data/conventions.md — schema style, migration rules, N+1 doctrine No new tool; SQL via shared code-mode themis docs/review/checklist.md — the gates actually enforced per project Secret scan is platform-level, not agent-owned prometheus docs/infra/conventions.md — CI stages, envs, containers, observability Observability absorbed from nyx ✓ hephaestus docs/ai/prompt-conventions.md (candidate — write when the project wires LLMs) No new tool nyx docs/testing/adversarial-corpus.md — the payloads that broke it, durable for the next run Fuzzing/adversarial niche — sole owner ✓ gaia geospatial conventions (candidate, niche deployments) Vision grant trio ✓ iris docs/release/runbook.md (candidate) — release steps gh actually runs gh workflows; never pushes/merges without human approval mnemosyne .pantheon/memory-bank/ + ADRs — owns it today memory_store grant — sole owner ✓ talos none — the hotfix lane stays light by design No tooling; speed is the product

The convention-doc rule (carried in each owning agent's body): keep the domain doc current as you work, read it first when it exists, propose it when the surface exists and the file does not — and update only what you changed; a stale convention line is worse than a missing one.

docs.title: Pantheon 2.0 — Modern Install, Settings UI, and Update Flow
docs.text: Status: design (approved direction, implementation queued as 2.0.x/2.1 work). References studied: opencode-quota, opencode-anon-turn, ECC, quire.sh, opencode-update-notifier, opencode-synced, opencode-usage-monitor, opencode-models-discovery, awesome-opencode, npm-12 script policy.

docs.title: 1. Install — the npx path dies for OpenCode 2.x
The happy path (matches opencode-quota exactly)
docs.text:
opencode plugin add pantheon-opencode        # npm, or a git URL
# restart OpenCode, then:
/pantheon Add CSV export to the reports page
  • One entry loads the server AND the TUI (our package already ships both).
  • Global via ~/.config/opencode; per-project via the project config.
  • Manual setup stays documented for people who edit opencode.json(c) themselves (one plugins entry, { package, options }).

docs.title: What happens to the installer
docs.text:
• npx pantheon-opencode init becomes the 1.x migration path only (the @4 init pattern quota uses for its legacy line), plus an opt-in project-scaffolding tool (agents/skills/commands copies, worktree box).
  • The 2.0 default flow never requires it. pantheon-opencode doctor, reconcile, and update survive as the maintenance CLI.
  • The V1→V2 config heal (singular plugin key → plural plugins, .ts path → directory) keeps running from both paths.
  • Beta.5: the wizard is gone. A TTY init is banner → per-file plan preview → ONE authorization (Apply these N changes?, default no). What the wizard used to ask lives in /pantheon-settings (gates, decision router, model preset, TUI personalization) or in explicit flags (--components, --project, --decision-model). The decision-layer extras prompt (which wrote ~/.config/pantheon/decision-flags.env) went with it — the env vars stay documented in docs/reference/env-vars.md and the J1 tab shows the names.

docs.title: 2. /pantheon-settings — the settings window
docs.text:
One window, one section per page, keyboard-first (tab cycles sections, esc/q closes — the whats-new and dispatch windows are the code templates). Every section writes to an existing mechanism; the UI is deterministic sugar, not a second brain. Shipped as of 2.0.0-beta.2:

Section Writes to Shipped in Gates & Overrides global pantheon-overrides.json (disable; replace content preserved across toggles; corrupt file refuses writes; project entries read-only) beta.1 / beta.2 guards Decision Model <config>/pantheon/decision-router.json enabled flag (schema v2 exact keys, 0600, applies live) beta.2 Model Preset <config>/opencode/.pantheon/active-preset.json (version-1 marker, .bak backup; none deletes) beta.2 J1 Risk Gate nothing — env-only config (PANTHEON_J1_*), status rows + restart hint beta.2 (status) Updates ~/.local/state/pantheon/update-check.json (Check now probes the registry dist-tag of the running channel) beta.2 Doctor nothing — file-derived health: install-version drift (H2), Node floor, overrides (K), decision-config validation beta.2 TUI host plugin storage (context.storage.store('tui-prefs') — durable, reactive): sidebar header lines/blocks, Context detail rows, gauge style, footer lines beta.5 About nothing beta.1

Deferred: Budgets (the ledger is SQLite — the fail-open window does not edit it), a J1 file surface (needs the runtime plugin to read a file at setup), and a persisted update-channel preference (needs the CLI update to honor it).

Expansion contract: a new setting = one entry in a registry + one row in a section, with the pure state in a TUI-local module (self-contained bundle doctrine) and a drift-pinning test against the canonical source. Nothing else moves. The window reads state through the same file shapes the plugin, installer and doctor consume — never a parallel format.

Non-goals: no config-file writer for arbitrary opencode.json keys (the host owns those); no server round-trips (everything is local file state); no credential, egress-consent or component wiring in the window (fail-open means the window never owns a step that can fail closed).

docs.title: 3. Updates — pin, notify, adopt deliberately
docs.text:
Doctrine (update-notifier + npm-12 reality + our own fail-closed culture): never silent auto-update. npm 12 blocks install scripts by default, and floating ranges are the supply-chain attack surface.

  • Pin by default: the installer/plugin add flow registers pantheon-opencode@<exact> — every upgrade is a reviewable config diff.
  • Notify: a lightweight registry check (npm dist-tag latest vs the pinned version, TTL-cached, offline-safe) surfaces ONE toast/sidebar line: "pantheon-opencode 2.0.1 available — changelog: …". This is the same surface as the existing whats-new window, which already announces per-version changes from CHANGELOG.md.
  • Adopt: pantheon-opencode update (already shipped) performs the bump with backup + reconcile; /pantheon-settings → About links the changelog.
  • Announce: releases keep the Keep-a-Changelog entry; the whats-new window renders it on first boot after upgrade. Beta channel unchanged (update prefers beta until stable is chosen).

docs.title: 4. Ecosystem alignment
docs.text: Concern Reference What we take Install + settings window opencode-quota one-command native install; tabbed window; npx only for the legacy line Install alternatives opencode-anon-turn git-URL and plugins-directory installs documented Multi-harness packaging ECC guided vs native setup separation; verified-channels warning Verification posture quire.sh verify-before-users-do — matches our evals/gates Update flow opencode-update-notifier pin + aggregate toast + deliberate adoption Config portability opencode-synced global-config-as-repo pattern (our managed regions already support it) Sidebar settings opencode-usage-monitor configurable refresh controls inside a sidebar Model discovery opencode-models-discovery provider/model filtering for the Models tab Ecosystem index awesome-opencode stay listed; watch the tui.json external-plugin loading caveat

docs.title: 5. Implementation order
docs.text:
1. Publish + install path — npm publish (dispatch), README/INSTALLATION switch to opencode plugin add, npx demoted to migrator (docs + CLI).
  2. Overrides wiring (Fase 3) — the Overrides tab needs the runtime consumer; do this first among features.
  3. /pantheon-settings, initial scope — Gates + Overrides + About tabs (all state exists today). Models + Budgets tabs follow with the preset and cap registries. ("initial" is the window's first iteration — the repo no longer uses v1/v2 labels for anything.)
  4. Update notifier — pinned-version check + toast, TTL cache, offline no-op; changelog link opens the whats-new window.
  5. Kill the npx default — remove it from README quick-starts; keep @1.x init documented as the legacy migration.

docs.title: Tutorial: Fast-Path CLI Utility with @talos
docs.text:
🇧🇷 Versão em Português disponível: Leia em Português

In this practical hands-on tutorial, you will learn how to use Pantheon's Fast Lane (@talos) to build a standalone, zero-dependency command-line utility with automated unit testing.

docs.title: Why Use the Fast Lane?
docs.text:
While complex features with database schemas and frontend interfaces benefit from @zeus and @athena's multi-phase Deepwork planning, everyday command-line tools, scripts, and bug fixes require speed and minimal ceremony.

flowchart LR
    subgraph StandardLane["🐢 Standard Orchestration Lane"]
        User1["👤 Developer"] --> Zeus["⚡ @zeus"]
        Zeus --> Athena["🏛️ @athena (Plan)"]
        Athena --> Hermes["✉️ @hermes"]
        Hermes --> Themis["⚖️ @themis (Audit)"]
    end

    subgraph FastLane["⚡ Fast Lane (@talos)"]
        User2["👤 Developer"] --> Talos["🛡️ @talos (Single-Turn Execution)"]
        Talos --> Result["✅ Done (Sub-second edit & test)"]
    end

@talos is Pantheon's specialized rapid responder: - No subagent overhead: Operates directly in the primary session. - Single-turn execution: Formulates code and runs tests immediately. - Fail-safe edits: Enforces strict syntax and test verification.

docs.title: 1. Project Goal: Repository Health Checker
docs.text: We will build a CLI utility named repo-health that analyzes any Git repository and outputs a score from 0 to 100 based on: 1. Git status: Clean working tree vs modified/untracked files. 2. Package manifest: Presence of package.json, valid JSON syntax, and test script. 3. Documentation: Presence of README.md.

docs.title: 2. Dispatching the Request to @talos
docs.text:
Start OpenCode and send this prompt:

@talos Create a zero-dependency CLI tool in Node.js at bin/repo-health.mjs that inspects the repository health:
1. Checks for uncommitted git changes.
2. Validates package.json syntax and checks for a "test" script.
3. Checks for README.md.
4. Outputs human-readable formatting by default and formatted JSON with --json flag.
5. Create comprehensive unit tests in tests/cli.test.mjs using node:test and node:assert.

docs.title: 3. Implementation Walkthrough
docs.text: @talos immediately writes the test suite and the implementation file.

docs.title: Step 3.1: Unit Test Suite (tests/cli.test.mjs)
docs.text:
Using Node.js native test runner (node:test):

import { describe, it } from 'node:test'
import assert from 'node:assert/strict'
import { checkRepoHealth } from '../bin/repo-health.mjs'

describe('checkRepoHealth', () => {
  it('returns a diagnostic result object with score and status', () => {
    const result = checkRepoHealth(process.cwd())

    assert.ok(typeof result.score === 'number', 'score should be a number')
    assert.ok(result.score >= 0 && result.score <= 100, 'score should be between 0 and 100')
    assert.ok(['EXCELENTE', 'REGULAR', 'CRÍTICO'].includes(result.status), 'status should be a valid tier')
    assert.ok(Array.isArray(result.issues), 'issues should be an array')
    assert.ok(typeof result.timestamp === 'string', 'timestamp should be ISO string')
  })

  it('correctly reports issues when package.json is missing in an empty directory', () => {
    const tempDir = process.env.TEMP || '/tmp'
    const result = checkRepoHealth(tempDir)

    assert.ok(result.issues.length > 0, 'should detect missing package.json or git repo')
    assert.ok(result.score < 100, 'score should be penalized')
  })
})

docs.title: Step 3.2: CLI Implementation (bin/repo-health.mjs)
docs.text:
#!/usr/bin/env node
import { execSync } from 'node:child_process'
import { existsSync, readFileSync } from 'node:fs'
import { join } from 'node:path'

export function checkRepoHealth(targetDir = process.cwd()) {
  const issues = []
  let score = 100

  // 1. Git status check
  try {
    const gitStatus = execSync('git status --porcelain', {
      cwd: targetDir,
      encoding: 'utf8',
    }).trim()
    if (gitStatus.length > 0) {
      const changedFiles = gitStatus.split('\n').length
      issues.push(`Warning: ${changedFiles} file(s) modified or untracked in Git`)
      score -= Math.min(20, changedFiles * 5)
    }
  } catch {
    issues.push('Alert: Directory is not a valid Git repository')
    score -= 40
  }

  // 2. Package manifest check
  const pkgPath = join(targetDir, 'package.json')
  if (existsSync(pkgPath)) {
    try {
      const pkg = JSON.parse(readFileSync(pkgPath, 'utf8'))
      if (!pkg.scripts?.test) {
        issues.push('Warning: package.json missing "test" script')
        score -= 15
      }
      if (!pkg.description || pkg.description.trim() === '') {
        issues.push('Warning: package.json has no description')
        score -= 5
      }
    } catch {
      issues.push('Error: package.json has invalid JSON syntax')
      score -= 30
    }
  } else {
    issues.push('Warning: package.json not found in root')
    score -= 20
  }

  // 3. Documentation check
  if (!existsSync(join(targetDir, 'README.md'))) {
    issues.push('Warning: README.md not found')
    score -= 15
  }

  const finalScore = Math.max(0, score)
  const status = finalScore >= 80 ? 'EXCELENTE' : finalScore >= 50 ? 'REGULAR' : 'CRÍTICO'

  return {
    score: finalScore,
    status,
    issues,
    timestamp: new Date().toISOString(),
  }
}

if (process.argv[1]?.endsWith('repo-health.mjs')) {
  const result = checkRepoHealth()
  const isJson = process.argv.includes('--json')

  if (isJson) {
    console.log(JSON.stringify(result, null, 2))
  } else {
    console.log('\n🏥 Pantheon Repo Health Diagnostic')
    console.log('──────────────────────────────────────')
    console.log(`Overall Score: ${result.score}/100 [${result.status}]`)
    if (result.issues.length === 0) {
      console.log('✅ No inconsistencies found. Clean repository!')
    } else {
      console.log('\nFindings:')
      for (const issue of result.issues) {
        console.log(`  • ${issue}`)
      }
    }
    console.log('')
  }
}

docs.text:

Output:

✔ checkRepoHealth > correctly reports issues when package.json is missing in an empty directory (4ms)
ℹ tests 2
ℹ suites 1
ℹ pass 2
ℹ fail 0

docs.title: Pantheon Cookbook: Everyday Practical Recipes
docs.text:
🇧🇷 Versão em Português disponível: Leia em Português

This practical cookbook aggregates the most common everyday development workflows with Pantheon, showcasing exact prompts, tool dispatches, and which specialist to call for each scenario.

docs.title: Recipe 1: Full-Stack Feature with TDD & Quality Gates
docs.text:
Scenario: Implement a complete feature (e.g., CSV export endpoint with schema validation and tests).

Prompt: 

@zeus Add CSV export support to /reports with unit tests and schema validation.

Workflow: 1. @zeus analyzes scope and delegates planning to @athena. 2. @athena defines phases and acceptance criteria; trade-offs are presented via the native question dialog. 3. Upon approval, @hermes writes failing tests (RED) and implements until green (GREEN). 4. @themis runs linters, security scans, and confirms coverage.

docs.title: Recipe 2: 1-Turn Express Hotfix (Bugs & Typos)
docs.text:
Scenario: Fix a CSS styling bug, a typo, or a missing import that does not require architectural ceremony.

Prompt: 

@talos Update the login submit button background from blue to emerald green in login.css

Why use @talos? @talos is Pantheon's fast lane. It operates without subagents, skips Deepwork planning ceremonies, executes surgical single-turn edits, and finishes immediately.

docs.title: Recipe 3: Database Migrations & Query Optimization
docs.text:
Scenario: Add a new table or column with proper indexing and foreign key constraints without N+1 query pitfalls.

Prompt: 

@demeter Create an Alembic migration adding the 'user_preferences' table with a foreign key to 'users' and an index on 'created_at'.

Why use @demeter? @demeter is Pantheon's persistence specialist. It enforces SQLAlchemy, Prisma, Alembic, and PostgreSQL best practices, ensuring referential integrity and optimized indexes.

docs.title: Recipe 4: Visual Refactoring from a Screenshot
docs.text:
Scenario: Rebuild or polish a frontend component to match a mockup.

Prompt: (Paste screenshot with Ctrl+V / Cmd+V into chat) 

@aphrodite Refactor this metrics card component to match the visual styling, spacing, and typography in the pasted screenshot.

Workflow: 1. Pantheon Vision processes the screenshot silently via session.context. 2. @aphrodite inspects colors, layout hierarchy, and typography, updating React and CSS components with WCAG AA compliance.

docs.title: Recipe 5: Safe Codebase Investigation (Read-Only)
docs.text:
Scenario: Understand complex logic across multiple files without risking unintended modifications.

Prompt: 

@apollo Search the repository and trace how authentication tokens are validated in incoming WebSocket connections.

Why use @apollo? @apollo is strictly read-only (edit: deny, bash: deny). It performs fast parallel exploration, returning structured findings with exact file paths and line ranges.

docs.title: Recipe 6: Pre-PR Quality & Security Audit
docs.text:
Scenario: Review all changes on the current branch before opening a pull request.

Prompt: 

@themis Audit all changes on this branch against OWASP Top 10 security standards, run Biome and test suites, and generate a quality verdict.

Why use @themis? @themis has read-only audit permissions (edit: deny). It never modifies code directly; it runs test suites, checks linting rules, and issues clear compliance verdicts (PASS, PASS_WITH_NOTES, BLOCK).

docs.title: Recipe 7: AI Pipelines and RAG Tooling
docs.text:
Scenario: Implement a semantic search service with vector embeddings.

Prompt: 

@hephaestus Implement a vector search pipeline using LangChain and pgvector for document chunk retrieval.

Why use @hephaestus? @hephaestus specializes in embeddings, vector stores, prompt chaining, and AI model integrations.

docs.title: Recipe 8: Docker & CI/CD Pipelines
docs.text:
Scenario: Create a multi-stage Dockerfile and a GitHub Actions workflow.

Prompt: 

@prometheus Create a multi-stage Dockerfile for our Node.js application and a GitHub Actions CI workflow to run tests on pull requests.

Why use @prometheus? @prometheus owns containerization, GitHub Actions, build automation, and infrastructure configurations.

docs.title: Recipe 9: Council Synthesis for Architecture Decisions (/pantheon)
docs.text:
Scenario: Arbitrate a technical trade-off across multiple architecture domains.

Prompt: 

/pantheon Should we use Server-Sent Events (SSE) or WebSockets for live status updates in our dashboard?

Why use /pantheon? Dispatches 2-3 specialists in parallel (@athena for architecture, @hermes for backend scalability, @themis for security and connection limits). Divergences are synthesized into a decisive recommendation with domain authority precedence.

docs.title: Recipe 10: Multi-Phase Project with Persistent Checkpoints (/pantheon-deepwork)
docs.text:
Scenario: Refactor a core system subsystem across multiple sessions without losing context.

Prompt: 

/pantheon-deepwork Migrate user session management from server-side memory to encrypted JWT cookies with redis blacklist.

Workflow: 1. Progress is written to .pantheon/deepwork/<slug>/ (plan.json, PLAN.md, checkpoints). 2. Parallel tasks execute in isolated git worktrees (.pantheon-worktrees/). 3. Each phase boundary requires a PASS verdict from @themis before progressing.

docs.title: Recipe 11: Interactive Question Gate in Complex Planning
docs.text:
Scenario: Clarify architectural ambiguities and design trade-offs interactively before code generation starts.

Workflow: When @athena designs a system with multiple valid approaches, @zeus presents the choices via OpenCode's native question tool: - The UI displays structured options with clear trade-offs. - A marked (Recommended) choice highlights the best-practice path. - The developer selects their preferred option, and execution proceeds automatically without textual back-and-forth.

docs.title: Recipe 12: Health Validation & Drift Detection (doctor)
docs.text:
Scenario: Verify that local MCP servers, plugins, and configurations are synchronized and healthy.

Command: 

npx pantheon-opencode doctor

When to run: - After git branch switches or pulling remote updates. - When upgrading Node.js or OpenCode. - If an MCP tool reports connection failures or missing dependencies.

docs.title: Deepwork: Disciplined Planning & Canonical Execution
docs.text:
🇧🇷 Versão em Português disponível: Leia em Português

Pantheon's Deepwork module is the architectural planning and disciplined execution engine for OpenCode. It solves the biggest issue with AI coding agents: the plan as an ephemeral Markdown document that the model reads, forgets, or prematurely concludes without verifiable proof.

docs.title: 1. Non-Negotiable Principles
docs.text:
1. JSON is Ground Truth, Markdown is a Projection: The canonical state lives in machine-verifiable, structured JSON (plan.json).
  2. Strictly Zero HTML: No scattered HTML pages or heavy dashboards. All approvals, prompts, and rejections use native OpenCode UI tools (question).
  3. Human Decisions First: Design trade-offs and open questions (decisions_needed) are resolved with the developer via interactive choice dialogs before execution.
  4. Dependency DAG, Not a Flat List: Tasks are connected in a Directed Acyclic Graph (Mermaid DAG), making parallel execution (parallel_safe) and blockers explicit.
  5. Fail-First Acceptance Criteria: Every task defines binary verification checks that currently fail (fails_now: true) and must pass upon completion.

docs.title: 2. Canonical On-Disk Structure
docs.text:
When a Deepwork workflow is initiated via /pantheon-deepwork or @zeus, Pantheon scaffolds a dedicated plan directory:

.pantheon/deepwork/<slug>/
├── plan.json        # Machine ground truth (strict JSON schema)
├── journal.ndjson   # Append-only audit log of phase and task transitions
└── PLAN.md          # Human-readable Markdown projection with Mermaid DAG

docs.title: The plan.json Format
docs.text:
{
  "plan_id": "PLAN_001_csv-export",
  "created_at": "2026-11-13T10:00:00Z",
  "intent": "Add asynchronous CSV metrics report export to the dashboard",
  "tier": "lite",
  "done_when": [
    "npm test tests/metrics-export.test.ts exits 0",
    "GET /api/reports/csv responds with Content-Type text/csv"
  ],
  "tasks": [
    {
      "task_id": "T1",
      "title": "Backend streaming CSV route",
      "owner": "@hermes",
      "depends_on": [],
      "parallel_safe": true,
      "verification": {
        "command": "node --test tests/metrics-api.test.mjs",
        "fails_now": true
      }
    },
    {
      "task_id": "T2",
      "title": "Export button with loading state",
      "owner": "@aphrodite",
      "depends_on": ["T1"],
      "parallel_safe": false,
      "verification": {
        "command": "npm test",
        "fails_now": true
      }
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: 3. Interactive Approval Gate with the question Tool
docs.text:
Open Questions are never dumped as plain text bullets in chat. Instead, @zeus extracts each decision into the native question tool:

[Interactive Question]
Which buffering approach should be used for CSV generation?
  • (Recommended) Native Node.js stream pipeline to prevent memory spikes
  • In-memory buffer serialization

Only after all required decisions are answered and the plan is approved does @zeus dispatch execution to specialist agents.

docs.title: 4. Visualizing Dependencies (Mermaid DAG)
docs.text:
Every PLAN.md automatically renders a Mermaid dependency graph:

graph TD
    T1["T1: Backend Streaming API (@hermes)"] --> T2["T2: Export UI Component (@aphrodite)"]
    T2 --> T3["T3: Quality & Security Audit (@themis)"]

docs.title: First Project Guide (End-to-End)
docs.text:
🇧🇷 Versão em Português disponível: Leia em Português

This practical guide walks you through using Pantheon step-by-step, from initializing a project to deploying with automated tests, quality gates, and telemetry.

docs.title: 1. What is Pantheon?
docs.text:
Pantheon is not a monolithic prompt or a generic chatbot: it is a multi-agent orchestration framework for OpenCode.

Rather than overloading a single model with architecture, backend, frontend, SQL, and testing, Pantheon delegates tasks to 14 specialized agents with clear boundaries and permissions.

flowchart TD
    User(["👤 Developer"]) -->|"/pantheon goal"| Zeus["⚡ @zeus (Orchestrator)"]

    Zeus -->|"Planning"| Athena["🏛️ @athena (Architect)"]
    Athena -->|"Code research"| Apollo["🔍 @apollo (Read-Only Scout)"]

    Athena -.->|"Plan with Interactive Questions"| User
    User -.->|"Approval via question tool"| Zeus

    Zeus -->|"Backend & APIs (TDD)"| Hermes["✉️ @hermes (Backend)"]
    Zeus -->|"Frontend & UI/UX"| Aphrodite["🎨 @aphrodite (Frontend)"]
    Zeus -->|"Migrations & SQL"| Demeter["🌾 @demeter (Database)"]

    Hermes & Aphrodite & Demeter -->|"Implementation ready"| Themis["⚖️ @themis (Auditor)"]
    Themis -->|"PASS / Verdict"| Zeus
    Zeus -->|"Delivery & Cost telemetry"| User

docs.title: 2. Step 1 — Installation and Setup
docs.text:
In any project directory (new or existing):

# Initialize Pantheon agents, skills, and plugins in the project
npx pantheon-opencode init

The interactive installer lets you choose components (agents, skills, instructions, plugins). Selecting plugins installs the modern TUI (terminal dashboard).

Verify installation health with the doctor diagnostic:

npx pantheon-opencode doctor

docs.title: 3. Step 2 — Dispatching Your First Feature
docs.text:
Start OpenCode (opencode) and invoke @zeus in chat:

@zeus Build a metrics dashboard service with:
1. Fastify backend with GET /api/metrics and GET /api/metrics/csv
2. React 19 UI with WCAG AA compliance and Tailwind styling
3. Automated unit tests with Node test runner

docs.title: 4. Step 3 — Architectural Planning with @athena
docs.text:
@zeus delegates the planning phase to @athena. @athena explores the repository using @apollo (read-only scout) and creates a canonical Deepwork plan (.pantheon/deepwork/<slug>/plan.json):

  • Structured Phases: Phase 1 (Backend API), Phase 2 (Frontend UI), Phase 3 (Audit & Validation).
  • Mermaid DAG: Shows parallel and sequential dependencies.
  • Fail-First Verification: Defines commands that fail now and must pass upon completion.

docs.title: Interactive Decision Gate (question tool)
docs.text:
When @athena identifies design trade-offs, @zeus immediately presents them using the native OpenCode question tool:

[Question Prompt]
Which CSV export streaming strategy should we adopt?
  1. (Recommended) Native Node.js stream pipeline to prevent memory spikes on large tables
  2. In-memory array serialization with Buffer

Once you select your choice and approve the plan, implementation begins.

docs.title: 5. Step 4 — Implementation via Specialists
docs.text: @zeus dispatches implementation tasks:

docs.title: 1. Backend via @hermes (TDD)
docs.text:
• Writes unit tests first in tests/metrics-api.test.mjs (RED): 
    import { describe, it } from 'node:test'
import assert from 'node:assert/strict'
import { getMetricsSnapshot } from '../src/server/metrics.mjs'

describe('Metrics Service', () => {
  it('returns valid metrics array', () => {
    const metrics = getMetricsSnapshot()
    assert.ok(Array.isArray(metrics), 'should be an array')
    assert.strictEqual(metrics.length, 4, 'should return 4 key metrics')
  })
})
  • Implements streaming CSV pipeline in src/server/metrics.mjs and Fastify routes in src/server/index.mjs (GREEN): 
    export function streamMetricsCsv(destination) {
  const items = getMetricsSnapshot()
  const header = 'id,name,category,value,unit,changePercent,updatedAt\n'
  const stream = new Readable({
    read() {
      this.push(header)
      for (const item of items) {
        this.push(`"${item.id}","${item.name}","${item.category}",${item.value},"${item.unit}",${item.changePercent},"${item.updatedAt}"\n`)
      }
      this.push(null)
    },
  })
  stream.pipe(destination)
}
  • Runs test suite: node --test tests/metrics-api.test.mjs passes 5/5.

docs.title: 2. Frontend via @aphrodite
docs.text:
• Implements accessible React 19 component: src/client/MetricsDashboard.jsx.
  • Ensures semantic markup, keyboard navigation, and WCAG AA contrast.

docs.title: 6. Step 5 — Security & Quality Audit with @themis
docs.text: Before finalizing, @zeus dispatches @themis to audit the changes: - Runs test suites and linters (npm test, npm run lint). - Verifies that no untrusted libraries or hardcoded secrets were introduced. - Evaluates test coverage and regression safety. - Issues a final PASS verdict.

docs.title: 7. Step 6 — Delivery & Cost Telemetry
docs.text:
@zeus summarizes the completed work with clickable file links:

  • Files Created: src/client/MetricsDashboard.jsx, src/server/index.mjs, src/server/metrics.mjs, tests/metrics-api.test.mjs.
  • Test Results: 5 passed, 0 failed.
  • Cost Summary: Tokens consumed, duration, and model provider efficiency.

docs.text: A complete implementation of this exact project is included in the Pantheon repository: - Check out examples/saas-dashboard/ to see the code, tests, and canonical Deepwork plan.

docs.title: Pantheon Vision: Visual Inspection and Multimodal Debugging
docs.text:
🇧🇷 Versão em Português disponível: Leia em Português

Pantheon Vision connects multimodal vision models to OpenCode, allowing you to paste screenshots, mockups, and UI layouts directly into chat for effortless implementation, debugging, and inspection.

docs.title: 1. Everyday Workflow
docs.text:
To inspect or refine an interface: 1. Capture a screenshot of the target screen, component, or visual bug. 2. In OpenCode (TUI or Desktop), paste the image from clipboard (Ctrl+V / Cmd+V). 3. Type your instructions naturally: 

Adjust this layout: build a responsive sidebar navigation matching these metrics

docs.title: 2. Zero Prompt Clutter (Clean Architecture)
docs.text:
In legacy versions, pasting an image injected raw comment blocks and temporary file paths directly into your message text:

<!-- pantheon-visual-context -->
[Visual] "clipboard" at "/tmp/pantheon-vision/6ef92982...png" · Q: '...' · relay session_id=...

In modern Pantheon: * Your message remains clean: The chat only shows the text you typed. * Silent Context Injection: Image references and metadata are injected directly through the session.context (system) hook. The agent receives full visual context behind the scenes without polluting chat history.

flowchart TD
    User(["👤 Developer"]) -->|"Pastes Screenshot (Ctrl+V)"| OpenCode["🖥️ OpenCode Interface"]
    OpenCode -->|"Plugin session.context hook"| VisionHook["👁️ Pantheon Vision Subsystem"]

    VisionHook --> ModelCheck{"Active Model supports Vision?"}
    ModelCheck -->|Yes| NativePass["Pass image directly to model via multimodal API"]
    ModelCheck -->|Text-only| FallbackServer["Invoke pantheon_vision MCP (describeImagesNative)"]

    FallbackServer --> StructuralDesc["Extract Layout, Text, Colors, and WCAG Metrics"]
    StructuralDesc --> SystemContext["Inject Structural Description into System Context"]
    NativePass --> SystemContext

    SystemContext --> Agent["🎨 @aphrodite (Frontend) / ⚡ @zeus"]
    Agent --> Implementation["Implement clean, accessible code with Zero Chat Pollution"]

docs.title: 3. Automatic Fallback for Text-Only Models
docs.text: If your active chat model does not natively support multimodal vision: * Pantheon does not fail or throw an unsupported model error. * Pantheon automatically delegates image inspection to the configured vision server (describeImagesNative / Zen Go), extracting layout structure, visible text, buttons, numbers, and color palettes. * The text model receives this high-fidelity description and implements the requested change seamlessly.

docs.title: 4. Configuring Your Vision Model
docs.text: You can configure which model handles visual inspection:

docs.title: Option A — Through the TUI
docs.text:
1. Open the TUI with pantheon tui.
  2. Go to the Settings tab ➔ Preset sub-tab.
  3. Select Vision Model (preset.vision_model).
  4. Choose from supported providers (e.g., gemini-2.5-flash, qwen3.7-vl, claude-3-5-sonnet).

docs.title: Option B — Via CLI
docs.text:
Configure the vision model directly from your terminal:

# List available vision-capable models
npx pantheon-opencode vision --list

# Set project-scoped vision model
npx pantheon-opencode vision --set opencode-go/gemini-2.5-flash

# Set globally for all projects
npx pantheon-opencode vision --global --set opencode-go/gemini-2.5-flash

Settings are persisted in .opencode/opencode-vision.json.

docs.text: Internal engineering record — not user guidance.

docs.title: Pre-release Changelog (1.6.0-beta.*)
docs.text: These sections were moved verbatim from CHANGELOG.md, newest first. Dates and order are unchanged.

docs.title: [v1.6.0-beta.18] - 2026-10-22
docs.text: • Persistence goal-schema initialization and migration guidance: a pristine project database now starts with both checkpoint and goal schemas; startup does not add goal DDL to an existing database. Existing-DB migration is only for users who want manual goal tools. When the schema is absent, the goal tools themselves return the exact migration command. User-facing guidance covers dry-run first, a stopped server, target confirmation, and verified 0600 backups.

docs.title: [v1.6.0-beta.17] - 2026-10-21
docs.text:
• Persistence MCP reduced to six registered tools: only context_save, context_get, and the four goal_* tools remain exposed; the twelve KV and context-management tools were unregistered while internal SQLite KV helpers remain for checkpoint storage. Goal tools are Zeus-only because goals are session-scoped and cannot be read across sessions, so Athena/Themis cannot read Zeus's goal or create one in their own root session.
  • Phase 7 — Memory search error contract: memory_search now returns a typed, sanitized error when the memory store cannot be read instead of an empty list; an empty result now means nothing matched. All-stopword queries previously fell back to a literal FTS match and now return no results, making the behavior uniform with queries whose stopwords are dropped.
  • Phase 8 — Memory MCP packaging: scripts/memory_mcp.py is now a thin shim delegating to canonical src/mcp/memory_mcp.py, removing the stale divergent copy; the sync test now asserts that their registered tool lists are equal.

docs.title: 🆕 What's New
docs.text: • V1 goal tools soft-deprecated: pantheon_goal_create, pantheon_goal_update, and pantheon_goal_get remain available with unchanged behavior, but stored legacy goals are not automatically continued in the current build. The durable manual replacement is the Persistence MCP goal_* surface available in this branch. Tool removal is deferred to a future release and requires explicit human approval.

docs.title: 🐞 Fixed
docs.text:
• Disabled goal loop does not suppress idle enforcement: hasActiveGoal now returns false while the loop is disabled, so stored legacy goals do not prevent the todo enforcer from receiving idle events.
  • Empty child-dispatch result is an explicit error: an empty result returned by a child dispatch is now surfaced as an error instead of being passed through as a normal result.

docs.title: ⚠️ Known Issues
docs.text:
• pantheon_cost aggregates by agent and phase: V1 reports both dimensions; V2 reports the literal phase unknown. The shipped tool has no per-session, per-model, per-provider or USD dimension; per-session aggregation exists only in the unpublished benchmark harness.
  • An empty child result can arrive as a completed call: the host supplies the placeholder Subagent completed without a text response.; Pantheon’s guard replaces the payload with its explicit error text, while the host’s completed status remains unchanged.
  • A user opencode.jsonc can change the effective plugin set: the host merges opencode.json with a sibling opencode.jsonc (scalars from .jsonc win, arrays are unioned), and Pantheon registers its plugin only in opencode.json.

docs.title: 🆕 What's New
docs.text:
• Safe memory handoffs and agent contracts: delegation briefs can pass minimized, non-sensitive memory references and takeaways as untrusted context; return formats and discovery/review routing are clarified across agent roles.
  • Optional per-session token breakdowns: benchmark reports can show root and descendant usage when session data is complete; incomplete data remains unavailable rather than being zero-filled.

docs.title: 🐞 Fixed
docs.text: • Empty task/subagent results: empty child-dispatch results are surfaced as explicit errors while non-empty structured results remain intact.

docs.title: [v1.6.0-beta.14] - 2026-10-17
docs.text: Published manually to npm on 2026-10-17; source commit and tag unknown.

docs.title: 🆕 What's New
docs.text:
• Installer model profiles: choose Inherit, OpenCode Go (hybrid), OpenAI, or Anthropic. Inherit leaves the active preset unset; OpenCode Go combines the premium lineup for Zeus, Athena, Themis, and Hephaestus with the Go lineup for other agents. Existing go-free, go-fast, and go-premium preset IDs remain available for compatibility.
  • Anthropic key guidance: the profile identifies ANTHROPIC_API_KEY as the required environment variable. The installer does not collect or inspect API keys; configure the key in your environment.
  • Modernized installer progress and terminal safety: Clack spinners are used in interactive TTYs, with readable output in headless/non-TTY runs. Canceling or selecting no components stops safely without writes; --no-mcp continues to exclude runtime, and --yes does not override an explicit decline.
  • Proportional delegation guidance: prompts now route bounded work directly to the relevant specialist and call for planning, broad discovery, review, or parallel work only when the request, uncertainty, dependencies, or risk warrant it.

docs.title: 🐞 Fixed
docs.text: • Reduce duplicated CI work: plugin V2 coverage now measures one focused TypeScript contract test while retaining its required 80% line-coverage threshold. The hook canary has one CI owner (test:node); its duplicate standalone CI invocation was removed. This records the CI configuration change, not a claim that the current CI run passed.

docs.title: 🆕 What's New
docs.text: • Modernize interactive TTY setup with @clack/prompts while keeping the existing component, install-location, authorization, and worktree guidance choices. Canceling the setup wizard leaves configuration unchanged; headless, --yes, dry-run, and non-TTY behavior remain available.

docs.title: 🐞 Fixed
docs.text:
• Let npm finish on an unsupported Node runtime: postinstall now warns and skips Node-dependent TUI/config sync, leaving the CLI to show its explicit Node >=26.4.0 hard gate and user-managed upgrade instructions.
  • Synchronize Beta 13 package and release metadata across manifests and lockfiles without changing the Node >=26.4.0 engine floor.

docs.title: 🆕 What's New
docs.text:
• Raise the Node.js support floor to 26.4.0 for the package, CLI, installer, and Node-based tooling. This release drops Node 22, Node 24, and Node 26.0–26.3; the npm beta dist-tag remains the intended publication channel.
  • Clarify runtime boundaries: this package requirement is not a universal OpenCode host-runtime claim. Official OpenCode V2.0.31 has a Bun runtime path and a separate Node build pinned to 26.4.0; no Bun minimum is asserted.
  • Keep node:sqlite as a separate capability threshold: Node >=22.5 may provide the optional pantheon_cost backend, but does not imply package support on that Node version.
  • Recommend a persistent external Git worktree location in interactive TTY setup summaries and the shipped worktrees skill. This is guidance only; Pantheon does not create worktrees or directories automatically.

docs.title: 🐞 Fixed
docs.text: • Synchronize Beta 12 version metadata and Node engine policy across package manifests, locks, citation/release metadata, CLI guards, doctor, and CI.

docs.title: 🆕 What's New

docs.title: 🐞 Fixed

docs.title: 🆕 What's New
docs.text:
• Visible plan approval: Zeus displays Athena's complete plan in the main conversation before requesting approval, including for /pantheon-deepwork.

  • OpenCode V2 Vision: adds vision_describe using the live image-capable model catalog and OpenCode Zen authentication; relative image paths resolve from the active project directory.

  • Menos contexto de instruções duplicadas no OpenCode V2: regras comuns entre as instruções globais e de projeto são emitidas uma vez, preservando regras exclusivas. Na medição intercalada do beta-10 com OpenCode v2.0.29, o proxy de contexto do primeiro request caiu 11,8%; input total e latência de parede permanecem inconclusivos.

  • Admissão segura de subagents no OpenCode V2: quando o host registra o hook de permissões, Pantheon correlaciona o agente, a sessão e o alvo do evento nativo subagent com o source da avaliação de permissão, antes da criação da sessão filha. A matriz permite Zeus→Apollo em uma sessão root e nega dispatches fora da matriz ou originados em uma sessão filha. A canary isolada passou em 18/18 verificações no OpenCode v2.0.29.

Evidência de F1 e F4A: bench/results/f1-di-v229-interleaved-2026-10-14.md e bench/results/f4a-v229-admission-identity-2026-10-14.md. O resultado de latência total e wall de F1 segue inconclusivo.

  • Especialista explícito como root no V2 (F3a): no cenário one-shot B, Talos iniciado explicitamente como agente root produziu o artefato correto sem child em 5/5 runs na amostra inicial. Um recheck de integração posterior encontrou 4/5; a instrução de Talos passou a exigir que arquivos pedidos sejam realmente gravados com a ferramenta nativa. Uma nova coorte pré-registrada passou em 5/5, sem children nem chamadas subagent. Nessa coorte, o proxy de contexto do primeiro request foi 9.675 tokens para Talos e 13.009 para Zeus (−25,6%, confirmado contra o spread intra-braço). Input total e wall permanecem sem claim de ganho; não há claim de economia monetária ou roteamento geral. O primeiro recheck e o follow-up são mantidos separadamente em bench/results/beta10-final-integration-2026-10-15.md e bench/results/beta10-final-integration-followup-2026-10-15.md; a evidência inicial está em bench/results/f3a-root-paired-2026-10-14.md.

  • Leitura bounded no OpenCode V2: adiciona pantheon_bounded_read para sessões root do Zeus, com aprovação nativa por arquivo, sem grant persistente, limites de chamadas/arquivos/linhas/bytes e scanner de segredos fail-closed. Validado no OpenCode v2.0.29; detalhes e limitações em bench/results/f3b-v229-bounded-read-2026-10-15.md.
