  ]
}

docs.title: 3. A Projeção Visual (PLAN.md)
docs.text: O arquivo PLAN.md projeta os dados do plan.json em um formato visual de fácil leitura para o desenvolvedor no editor ou terminal:

docs.title: Exemplo de Grafo de Execução gerado:
docs.text:
graph TD
    T1["T1: Testes de Contrato (@hermes)"] --> T2["T2: Gerador de Stream (@hermes)"]
    T2 --> T3["T3: Botão na UI (@aphrodite)"]
    D1{{"Decisão D1: UTF-8 BOM"}} -.->|bloqueia| T2

    classDef done fill:#22c55e,stroke:#15803d,color:#fff;
    classDef active fill:#3b82f6,stroke:#1d4ed8,color:#fff;
    classDef pending fill:#64748b,stroke:#475569,color:#fff;

docs.title: 4. O Portão de Decisões Interativo (question)
docs.text: Toda vez que o plano contiver itens em decisions_needed ou Open Questions: * O Zeus e a Athena são proibidos de prosseguir às cegas. * O OpenCode abre a caixa de diálogo interativa na tela (question tool). * Cada decisão é respondida com 1 clique. * O evento de resposta é registrado no journal.ndjson com timestamp, liberando as tarefas dependentes.

docs.title: 5. Como Iniciar um Plano Deepwork
docs.text:
No chat do OpenCode:

/pantheon-deepwork Refatorar módulo de autenticação para suportar login por Passkey

Ou pedindo diretamente para o Zeus:

@zeus elabore um plano de deepwork para a issue #304

O plano é sintetizado pela @athena, auditado pela @themis e apresentado a você para aprovação com links clicáveis file:// para os arquivos gerados.

docs.title: Guia do Primeiro Projeto (End-to-End)
docs.text:
🇺🇸 English version available: Read in English

Este guia ensina a utilizar o Pantheon na prática, passo a passo, desde a inicialização de um projeto novo até o deploy final com testes, portões de qualidade e telemetria de custos.

docs.title: 1. O que é o Pantheon?
docs.text:
O Pantheon não é um prompt gigante nem um assistente genérico: ele é um framework de orquestração multi-agente para o OpenCode.

Em vez de sobrecarregar um único modelo com planejamento, código backend, CSS, banco de dados e testes, o Pantheon divide o trabalho entre 14 agentes especialistas com permissões e papéis rigorosamente demarcados.

flowchart TD
    User(["👤 Desenvolvedor"]) -->|"/pantheon objetivo"| Zeus["⚡ @zeus (Orquestrador)"]

    Zeus -->|"Planejamento"| Athena["🏛️ @athena (Arquiteta)"]
    Athena -->|"Pesquisa de código"| Apollo["🔍 @apollo (Batedor Read-Only)"]

    Athena -.->|"Plano com Perguntas Interativas"| User
    User -.->|"Aprovação via question tool"| Zeus

    Zeus -->|"Backend & APIs (TDD)"| Hermes["✉️ @hermes (Backend)"]
    Zeus -->|"Frontend & UI/UX"| Aphrodite["🎨 @aphrodite (Frontend)"]
    Zeus -->|"Migrations & SQL"| Demeter["🌾 @demeter (Database)"]

    Hermes & Aphrodite & Demeter -->|"Código pronto"| Themis["⚖️ @themis (Auditora)"]
    Themis -->|"PASS / Veredicto"| Zeus
    Zeus -->|"Entrega e métricas de custo"| User

docs.title: 2. Passo 1 — Instalação e Inicialização
docs.text:
Em qualquer pasta de projeto (nova ou existente):

# Inicializa os agentes, skills e plugins do Pantheon no projeto
npx pantheon-opencode init

O instalador interativo permite selecionar componentes (agents, skills, instructions, plugins). A opção plugins instala a TUI (interface de terminal moderna).

Verifique se tudo está íntegro executando o diagnóstico de integridade:

npx pantheon-opencode doctor

Se o doctor relatar 0 warnings, seu ambiente está pronto!

docs.title: 3. Passo 2 — Abrindo o OpenCode e a TUI
docs.text:
Abra sua sessão do OpenCode:

opencode

Se você instalou a TUI, você verá a barra lateral com: * Context Gauge: Consumo de tokens da janela de contexto em tempo real. * Spend / Cost: Custo acumulado da sessão em dólares (\$USD). * Git Status: Branch atual e status do repositório. * Active Preset: Preset de modelos ativo (balanced, quality, speed ou customizado).

docs.title: 4. Passo 3 — Disparando sua Primeira Tarefa com o Zeus
docs.text:
No chat do OpenCode, fale com o coordenador @zeus usando o comando /pantheon:

/pantheon Criar um painel de monitoramento de métricas em React com exportação de relatórios em CSV e endpoint backend com testes unitários.

docs.title: O que o Zeus faz:
docs.text:
1. Analisa o escopo: Se a tarefa for complexa ou envolver múltiplos subsistemas, o Zeus aciona a @athena para estruturar um plano formal.
  2. Athena pesquisa o projeto: A Athena consulta o @apollo para ler arquivos e dependências sem poluir o contexto da conversa.
  3. Plano Deepwork gerado: A Athena devolve o plano canônico com DAG de dependências em Mermaid e lista de arquivos afetados.

docs.title: 5. Passo 4 — O Portão de Perguntas e Aprovação (question)
docs.text:
Quando o plano contém incertezas técnicas ou escolhas arquiteturais, o Pantheon nunca deixa perguntas soltas como texto morto:

Aparece na sua tela o diálogo nativo interativo do OpenCode (question tool):

? Escolha o formato da exportação CSV:
  ▸ (Recomendado) Streaming assíncrono com cabeçalho UTF-8 (menor consumo de RAM)
    Geração síncrona em memória (Buffer)

? Aprovar plano e iniciar execução?
  ▸ (Recomendado) Aprovar e iniciar execução
    Ajustar plano

Com as setas do teclado e Enter, você responde em 3 segundos. Suas escolhas são registradas no histórico auditável e o Zeus prossegue imediatamente.

docs.title: 6. Passo 5 — Implementação em TDD pelos Especialistas
docs.text:
O Zeus agora despacha as tarefas em paralelo ou em sequência:

  • Backend com @hermes (TDD):
  • Escreve os testes unitários primeiro em tests/metrics-api.test.mjs (RED): 
    import { describe, it } from 'node:test'
import assert from 'node:assert/strict'
import { getMetricsSnapshot } from '../src/server/metrics.mjs'

describe('Metrics Service', () => {
  it('retorna array de métricas válido', () => {
    const metrics = getMetricsSnapshot()
    assert.ok(Array.isArray(metrics), 'deve ser um array')
    assert.strictEqual(metrics.length, 4, 'deve retornar 4 métricas chave')
  })
})
  • Implementa a lógica e streaming em src/server/metrics.mjs (GREEN): 
    export function streamMetricsCsv(destination) {
  const items = getMetricsSnapshot()
  const header = 'id,name,category,value,unit,changePercent,updatedAt\n'
  const stream = new Readable({
    read() {
      this.push(header)
      for (const item of items) {
        this.push(`"${item.id}","${item.name}","${item.category}",${item.value},"${item.unit}",${item.changePercent},"${item.updatedAt}"\n`)
      }
      this.push(null)
    },
  })
  stream.pipe(destination)
}

  • Roda os testes: node --test tests/metrics-api.test.mjs passa 5/5.

  • Frontend com @aphrodite:

  • Cria o componente visual (src/client/MetricsDashboard.jsx).
  • Aplica Tailwind CSS com suporte a dark mode, navegação por teclado e conformidade WCAG AA.
  • Adiciona botão de download com feedback visual de progresso.

docs.title: 7. Passo 6 — Portão de Qualidade e Segurança com @themis
docs.text: Antes de concluir a entrega, o Zeus aciona a @themis: * A Themis executa os linters (npm run lint / Biome / Ruff). * Executa a suite de testes automatizados (npm test). * Valida ausência de segredos ou vulnerabilidades OWASP. * Emite o relatório de veredito: PASS.

docs.title: 8. Passo 7 — Verificando Custos e Métricas
docs.text:
Ao final da execução, verifique a telemetria do trabalho executado:

/pantheon_cost

O comando exibe: * Tokens de entrada e saída consumidos por modelo. * Cache hit rate (economia de tokens por cache de prompt). * Duração da sessão e custo total formatado em USD (\$0.04).

docs.title: 9. Próximos Passos
docs.text:
• Matriz de Capacidades dos Agentes — Saiba detalhadamente o que cada agente pode e não pode fazer.
  • Deepwork Architecture — Como funciona o motor de planos em JSON e DAGs.
  • Pantheon Vision — Como colar capturas de tela e depurar interfaces visuais.
  • Cookbook de Receitas — Casos práticos prontos para o seu dia a dia.

docs.title: Pantheon Vision: Análise Visual e Inspeção de Telas
docs.text:
🇺🇸 English version available: Read in English

O Pantheon Vision conecta modelos multimodais de visão computacional ao OpenCode, permitindo que você compartilhe capturas de tela, designs e layouts para implementação, depuração e inspeção sem atrito.

docs.title: 1. Como Usar no Dia a Dia
docs.text:
Para inspecionar ou ajustar uma interface: 1. Tire uma captura de tela da tela ou do componente com erro/design desejado. 2. No OpenCode (TUI ou Desktop), cole a imagem da área de transferência (Ctrl+V / Cmd+V). 3. Digite sua instrução: 

ajustar isso daqui, criar um menu lateral responsivo e atualizar as métricas

docs.title: 2. Zero Artefatos no Chat (Arquitetura Limpa)
docs.text:
Nas versões legadas, colar uma imagem costumava injetar blocos confusos de texto e comentários HTML no meio da sua mensagem:

<!-- pantheon-v2-visual-context -->
[Visual] "clipboard" at "/tmp/pantheon-vision/6ef92982...png" · Q: '...' · relay session_id=...

Na versão moderna do Pantheon: * Sua mensagem permanece 100% limpa: A interface exibe apenas o texto que você digitou. * Injeção Silenciosa em Contexto de Sistema: As referências da imagem e os metadados de inspeção são injetados diretamente no hook session.context (system). O modelo de IA recebe todas as instruções nos bastidores, sem poluir visualmente a conversa.

flowchart TD
    User(["👤 Desenvolvedor"]) -->|"Cola Screenshot (Ctrl+V)"| OpenCode["🖥️ Interface do OpenCode"]
    OpenCode -->|"Hook de plugin session.context"| VisionHook["👁️ Subsistema Pantheon Vision"]

    VisionHook --> ModelCheck{"Modelo ativo suporta Visão?"}
    ModelCheck -->|Sim| NativePass["Envia imagem diretamente pela API multimodal"]
    ModelCheck -->|Puramente Textual| FallbackServer["Aciona MCP pantheon_vision (describeImagesNative)"]

    FallbackServer --> StructuralDesc["Extrai Estrutura, Textos, Cores e Métricas WCAG"]
    StructuralDesc --> SystemContext["Injeta Descrição Estruturada no Contexto de Sistema"]
    NativePass --> SystemContext

    SystemContext --> Agent["🎨 @aphrodite (Frontend) / ⚡ @zeus"]
    Agent --> Implementation["Implementa o código acessível com Zero Poluição no Chat"]

docs.title: 3. Fallback Automático para Modelos Textuais
docs.text: Se você estiver utilizando um modelo principal que é puramente textual (ou cujo gateway não aceita imagens diretamente): * O Pantheon não falha e não responde que é incapaz de ler a imagem. * O Pantheon invoca automaticamente o servidor multimodal configurado (describeImagesNative / Zen Go), extrai a descrição estruturada da interface (layout, textos visíveis, botões, métricas numéricas e cores) e entrega ao modelo textual. * O modelo textual passa a "enxergar" a tela por meio da descrição de alta fidelidade e prossegue com a implementação normalmente.

docs.title: 4. Configurando seu Modelo de Visão Preferido
docs.text: Você pode escolher qual modelo realiza a inspeção de imagens:

docs.title: Opção A — Pela TUI (Interface Gráfica de Terminal)
docs.text:
1. Abra a TUI com pantheon tui ou acesse a aba de configurações.
  2. Navegue até a aba Settings ➔ sub-aba Preset.
  3. Localize a linha Vision Model (preset.vision_model).
  4. Alterne para o modelo desejado (padrão auto, opencode-go/mimo-v2.6-flash, anthropic/claude-3-5-sonnet, google/gemini-2.5-flash, etc.).
  5. As alterações são salvas automaticamente no arquivo canônico opencode-vision.json.

docs.title: Opção B — Via Arquivo de Configuração
docs.text:
Crie ou edite .opencode/opencode-vision.json no seu projeto:

{
  "visionModel": "opencode-go/mimo-v2.6-flash"
}

docs.title: Opção C — Via Variável de Ambiente
docs.text: export PANTHEON_VISION_MODEL="opencode-go/mimo-v2.6-flash"

docs.title: 5. Boas Práticas ao Trabalhar com a @aphrodite (Frontend)
docs.text: Ao enviar imagens para alterações visuais: * Uma imagem é contexto, não autorização para reverter trabalho: A @aphrodite compara a imagem com a UI existente e preserva o código funcional já implementado. * Declare a intenção: Indique se a imagem é um design desejado (mockup), um bug visual em produção ou uma referência estética de inspiração. * Acessibilidade primeiro: Ao implementar uma tela baseada em imagem, a @aphrodite sempre aplica conformidade com WCAG (contraste adequado, tags semânticas e acessibilidade de teclado).

docs.title: Code Mode
docs.text:
Code Mode runs scripts through the pantheon-code-mode MCP server (execute_code_script). A script runs only when it is explicitly approved. Approval is recorded in .pantheon/code-mode/manifest.json with the SHA-256 of each script:

{
  "version": 1,
  "scripts": {
    "example-sync.sh": "<sha256>"
  }
}

docs.title: Approval rules
docs.text:
• No manifest → nothing executes. A missing manifest returns INVALID_STATE; scripts are never run implicitly.
  • Not listed → CONFLICT. The script must be approved first.
  • Hash mismatch → CORRUPT_DATA. The SHA-256 of the file on disk must match the manifest entry, so edits after approval are detected.

Approve or re-approve a script with the approve_code_script MCP tool:

approve_code_script("checkpoint-session.sh")

The installer seeds the manifest with the SHA-256 of every bundled script, so shipped scripts stay approved across installs. Re-run approve_code_script after intentionally editing a script.

Only .sh and .py files are allowed. Execution has a 30-second timeout, and path traversal outside the code-mode directory is blocked.

docs.title: Resolution
docs.text: Code Mode resolves project-first: .opencode/.pantheon/code-mode is preferred, then .pantheon/code-mode. PANTHEON_PROJECT overrides the working directory, and the installed MCP uses cwd: "." so OpenCode supplies the workspace. A global directory is used only when no usable project directory is available. Once a project directory is selected, a missing or corrupt manifest fails closed instead of falling back. doctor validates the manifest and every script's SHA-256 without regenerating it.

docs.title: Status codes
docs.text: Results use the shared nine-code contract: OK, UNSUPPORTED, UNAVAILABLE, INVALID_INPUT, INVALID_STATE, CONFLICT, CORRUPT_DATA, TIMEOUT, ESCALATE. With json_output=true, results carry a status field.

docs.title: Persistence is separate
docs.text: Session persistence is provided by the Persistence MCP server. The bundled code-mode payload contains execution helpers only and does not export or back up a database. See Memory.

docs.title: Development assets
docs.text:
The local .pantheon/code-mode/eval-*.py helpers and any Promptfoo/evaluation assets are development-only inputs. They are excluded from the npm tarball and from the runtime manifest. src/mcp/eval_store.py is different: it is a shipped runtime dependency of the MCP resources server, not an evaluation asset, so it remains packaged.

Server setup and the tool reference are in MCP and MCP Tools.

docs.title: Environment Variables
docs.text: Only variables that change Pantheon behavior are listed. Test-only and internal diagnostic variables are not user knobs. Values are read at process start unless noted.

docs.title: Installer and generation
docs.text:
Variable Default Purpose OPENCODE_VERSION unset v2 pins the host gate and skips the probe. Any other value — including v1 — is refused. OPENCODE_BIN opencode Host binary used for the --version probe. A basename of opencode2 resolves to 2.x without probing. OPENCODE_V2_SPEC @opencode/cli@latest Sandbox spec that provides the opencode2 binary.

The host gate is described once in Compatibility.

docs.title: Sandbox runs
docs.text:
Variable Default Purpose PANTHEON_SANDBOX_ROOT ~/pantheon-sandbox Isolated sandbox root. Refused if unsafe for --reset. PANTHEON_SANDBOX_MODEL opencode-go/mimo-v2.5 Model used by init and the prompt battery. PANTHEON_PROMPT_TIMEOUT 300 Per-prompt timeout in seconds.

Sandbox mechanics are in Release Process.

docs.title: Paths and storage
docs.text: Variable Default Purpose PANTHEON_HOME unset Overrides the config root used for memory and the price cache. Resolution is PANTHEON_HOME, else $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/opencode, else ~/.config/opencode. XDG_CONFIG_HOME ~/.config Used when PANTHEON_HOME is unset. XDG_STATE_HOME ~/.local/state User state root for the separate local decision-budget SQLite ledger. PANTHEON_PROJECT unset Absolute project root for project-first resolution (code mode, persistence). A relative value is rejected where an absolute path is required. PANTHEON_HOOKS_LOG <project>/.pantheon/logs/hooks.log Overrides the plugin hook log path.

docs.title: Memory
docs.text:
Variable Default Purpose PANTHEON_MEMORY_MAX_ENTRY_BYTES 65536 Per-entry serialized size cap for memory_store. Any positive integer; an invalid value falls back to 64 KiB. Read per write.

Memory policy is in Memory.

docs.title: Cost
docs.text:
Variable Default Purpose PANTHEON_NODE node from PATH Node >= 22.5 binary used only for the node:sqlite capability in the CLI fallback. Must exist and be executable. PANTHEON_COST_OFFLINE unset Set to 1 to forbid every network request, including refreshPricing: true. No socket is opened. PANTHEON_COST_DB unset Absolute path to the cost database, checked before OPENCODE_DB. OPENCODE_DB unset Absolute path to the cost database, checked before the XDG default. PANTHEON_OPENCODE_VERSION unset v1 or v2 narrows an already-detected schema to one table family. It does not select a file.

Backend resolution and report dimensions are in MCP Tools.

docs.title: Vision
docs.text:
Variable Default Purpose PANTHEON_VISION_MODEL unset Highest-precedence vision model pin. An explicit pin that does not qualify (non-Zen, text-only, or absent from the catalog) is discarded and automatic selection takes over. PANTHEON_OPENCODE_API_KEY unset OpenCode Zen credential for native vision and the vision MCP. OPENCODE_API_KEY unset Shared fallback credential for Zen endpoints. PANTHEON_VISION_TOOL unset Opts into the Bifrost vision tool; Bifrost is never the default.

Model precedence and the degradation chain are in MCP.

docs.title: Models
docs.text: Variable Default Purpose PANTHEON_MODEL_PRESET unset Legacy preset selector. The runtime ignores static presets and applies only explicit per-agent project overrides.

docs.title: Local decision recommendation
docs.text:
Variable Default Purpose PANTHEON_LOCAL_DECISION_ROUTER unset (disabled) Set to 1 to enable only the standalone local advisory API. It does not enable provider transport, host dispatch, or permissions.

The API contract and its abstention behavior are in Local Decision Router.

docs.title: Decision layer flags (shadow adapters)
docs.text:
All four flags are read once when the plugin registers, so changing any of them needs a host restart. None is set in a default install; anything other than the listed truthy values leaves the feature off.

Variable Default Purpose PANTHEON_V2_P7_LOOP unset (off) 1, on or true enables the P7 loop adapter on session.execution.succeeded. It counts executions and writes effect: none observations to an in-memory, bounded collector that the plugin never reads back (it is exposed only to tests); it does not enforce loop limits. The 12-execution cap (P7_LOOP_MAX_EXECUTIONS) is advisory: no measured host surface signals a new user turn, so the streak is not claimed to reset. PANTHEON_V2_P8_GUARDRAIL unset (off) 1, on or true would enable the P8 guardrail on permission.evaluate only. It can only narrow, and it remains off: C8 closed by measurement, and the verdict is that the declared rules match no delivered payload, so the point is recorded as advisory and narrows nothing. A written deny is honoured by the host, but no declared rule can produce one. execute.before remains the only hard barrier. PANTHEON_J1_RISK_SCORE unset (off) 1, on or true enables the J1 risk-score shadow gate on execute.before for write/execute tool calls (bash/shell and webfetch, file writes). Each observed call fires ONE bounded native Jev decision through the same gate chain as pantheon_jev_decide (config, consent, budget reservation, decision.egress permission) and records effect: none shadow records (reason tokens like risk-3-intent-yes, skip-timeout) to the in-memory, bounded collector the plugin never reads back. The request carries no user content: tool name token, scope class and the tool input's sha256 only. Fail-open on every failure mode; fired without awaiting the hook, self-bounded at 2s, never retried. Shadow never blocks — the only reachable verdict is observe. See V2 Native Decisions. PANTHEON_J3_ESCALATION unset (off) 1, on or true enables the J3 turn-complexity escalation shadow classifier on execute.before for delegate dispatches (the native subagent tool). Each dispatch fires ONE bounded native Jev decision through the same gate chain as pantheon_jev_decide (config, consent, budget reservation, decision.egress permission) asking one score question ("complexity of this delegation", 2–10 levels) and records effect: none shadow records (reason tokens like esc-cheap-c2, esc-main-c-na, skip-timeout). The request carries no user content: delegate agent token, Brief sha256, Brief length and the local risk-word flag only — the Brief text never leaves the machine. Local rails (risk words, user-pinned model, >8,000-char Brief) and every unsure or timed-out answer force the main model. Shadow only: the recorded verdict never changes the dispatched model in this phase — the per-agent override mechanism exists behind a tested seam for a separately reviewed activation. Fired without awaiting the hook, self-bounded at 2s, never retried. See V2 Native Decisions.

Shadow points (P1, P2, P3, P9, P11) have no environment switch: there is no behaviour to switch. P1 and P2 are registered on session.hook('prompt') and observe a projection of the admission payload carrying only prompt.agents and prompt.skills — no text, no file bytes, no metadata. P3 is registered at its declared tool.invoke: the pantheon_local_decision tool hands the adapter its own input, which carries complexity and gateStatus, so it records a classification when the tool is invoked. P9 is registered on session.hook('compaction') and reads the measured carrier only — the top-level sessionID and the system parts — pushing nothing into the injected context. P11 is registered inside ctx.tool.transform and reads the draft the host hands it without calling any mutator. Each record says effect: none and goes to an in-memory, bounded collector that the plugin never reads back (exposed only to tests). They cannot deny, delay or mutate admission; P2 stays advisory and never filters.

The remaining four — P4, P5, P6 and P10 — have no production call site: no production file imports them. Their adapters are constructed only by their per-point test suites (v2-decision-p4.test.ts … v2-decision-p11.test.ts). P6 and P10 declared the prompt hook, but that payload carries neither council candidates nor counsellor claims; P4 needs a memory candidate array and the measured context payload carries system text parts instead; P5 needs a declared { requirements, responses } pair and the execute.after event carries neither. They are unwired rather than recording a refusal from a surface that cannot feed them. On a host they do not read the turn, record no telemetry and change nothing — not because they are disabled, but because nothing constructs them. Coverage and unmeasured surfaces are in Local Decision Router.

docs.title: Decision-provider credentials
docs.text:
There is no Pantheon-owned decision transport. The only egress surface is the host's native Decisions API, invoked by the explicit pantheon_jev_decide tool behind the user-level config, budget, and permission gates — see V2 Native Decisions. The variables below are listed because decision-router code mentions them; none is read on a production path.

Variable Default Purpose OPENAI_API_KEY unset Not read anywhere. Direct OpenAI has no native Decisions route and is never substituted. TYPESAFE_API_KEY unset Not read anywhere. The native TypeSafe route uses host-owned /connect credentials, never a Pantheon env read. OPENCODE_API_KEY unset Not read by the decision router for OpenCode Console/Free; the native route uses the host's own Console auth. It remains in use by other documented OpenCode integrations.

There is no configurable base URL, retry, failover, or fan-out switch, and caps have no defaults. The request bound (one bounded text state, 1–4 typed questions) lives in the native request preparer; a denied host permission means zero requests.

docs.title: Runtime-specific
docs.text: Variable Default Purpose OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_BACKGROUND_SUBAGENTS unset Experimental gate for some runtimes; set by Pantheon's npm run start launcher. It is not a universal prerequisite and does not create a missing tool.

docs.title: What is not here
docs.text: Local Promptfoo/evaluation experiments are development-only: place them under evals/promptfoo/, which is gitignored and excluded from packaging, package evidence, CI tests, coverage, and release gates. Publish reviewed findings as documentation, not the harness, datasets, outputs, or credentials.

docs.title: Local decision recommendation API
docs.text:
Current status: Deterministic local per-turn recommendations are active in the prompt hook when the user-level enabled preference is true. They are advisory: the hook can add a local marker and only narrow an existing skill array when identifiable IDs overlap; it never dispatches agents or changes permissions or approvals. The former direct-provider branch is detached and inactive regardless of legacy consent, caps, provider selection, or credentials. Native Decisions have exactly one production call site: the explicit, Zeus-only pantheon_jev_decide tool through the host's native API, behind the full consent/budget/permission chain. The per-turn hook makes no native call. See the V2 native Decisions status.

The pantheon-opencode/local-decision-router export is an opt-in, deterministic local advisory API. PANTHEON_LOCAL_DECISION_ROUTER=1 enables only that local selector. The plugin exposes a separate pantheon_local_decision advisory tool; it does not intercept or replace native subagent dispatch. An abstention or recommendation does not start work, change grants, authorize shell, or relax a review/approval gate.

docs.title: Per-turn local recommendation (active)
docs.text: When the user-level enabled preference is true, the production prompt hook uses the deterministic local skill selector and current local routing policy on the user's current request text. It may append a pantheon-decision-router:v1 advisory marker and narrow prompt.skills only when the host supplies a non-empty array containing identifiable skill IDs that overlap the selection; absent, empty, unidentifiable, or disjoint lists are left intact. This selector does not require provider consent, credentials, caps, a permission assertion, or a network request. Its agent recommendation is advisory only and never dispatches a specialist, changes grants, authorizes shell, or relaxes an approval gate. The manual advisory API/tool remain separate.

docs.title: Historical direct-provider route (removed)
docs.text: Earlier revisions also documented direct-provider calls from the prompt path. That branch was detached from the production hook and has since been removed entirely (runner, payload protocol, and fetch-path usage verifier). Legacy consent, caps, period, provider selection, credentials, and permission settings do not bring it back: there is no Pantheon-owned transport left to wire.

docs.title: Local orchestration advisory
docs.text:
The Zeus-context-gated tool accepts only structured candidate agent/skill/ resource IDs, a nullable exact specialist domain, complexity dimensions, a gate status, and a boolean indicating whether prior history may matter. It reads local routing.yml metadata (parsed once per process; read failures are not cached and retry on the next call) and returns a typed recommendation or abstention. Candidate agents are intersected with Zeus's current routing list, permission.task rules, canonical agent IDs, and the caller-supplied set of currently available native subagent targets. Skills are intersected with the selected agent's routing skill list; resource recommendations are restricted to known Pantheon resource IDs. The caller must supply candidates from the live host schema and currently available skill/resource set; the tool does not inspect or grant host permissions. Plugin tool registration is global and does not expose per-agent visibility; therefore the tool checks the host-supplied context.agent at execution and returns abstention for every non-Zeus or identity-missing call. The selector is never an authorization boundary for the native dispatch.

Use it selectively for genuinely ambiguous delegation choices. Obvious work goes directly to the native subagent tool without calling this selector, Jev, council, or Athena planning solely for confirmation. A result is advisory: Zeus validates it again and builds the Brief locally. The boolean may prompt a single selective local pantheon-memory search, but the tool performs no search and receives no task text, transcript, memory/resource contents, files, credentials, or secrets. Memory search, read-only resources, and persistence checkpoints remain distinct systems. The selector may recommend a skill/resource ID but never invokes it. The adapter does not replace native delegation.

docs.title: Enablement
docs.text:
The standalone local API is disabled unless PANTHEON_LOCAL_DECISION_ROUTER=1 is present when the process calls it. Unset, empty, and any other value leave it disabled. When disabled, it returns decision: "abstain" and reasonCode: "DISABLED".

The user-level enabled flag and decision-router enable/disable commands control the local per-turn recommendation only. They do not activate direct- provider egress; no combination of legacy provider/consent/budget settings does.

docs.title: User-level settings and budget tooling
docs.text:
The provider, model, consent, cap, period, and ledger commands manage stored administrative state. The enabled preference alone is consulted by the local per-turn recommendation. The remaining state additionally gates the explicit native pantheon_jev_decide tool: egress requires enabled, egress_consent, exactly one cap-valid native candidate, and a confirmed budget period in the ledger. Those settings still do not activate any per-turn provider egress. Native candidate mapping and the full gate chain are documented in V2 native Decisions.

Runtime preferences and caps are user-level, not project-level and not OpenCode global configuration. The non-secret JSON file is $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/pantheon/decision-router.json (default ~/.config/pantheon/decision-router.json) and is written with mode 0600 under a private 0700 Pantheon directory. The separate SQLite admission ledger is $XDG_STATE_HOME/pantheon/decision-budget.sqlite (default ~/.local/state/pantheon/decision-budget.sqlite), also user-owned/private. Neither file stores API credentials. The installer may retain a legacy target preference; it is not runtime authority. Only this user-level configuration is consulted.

npx pantheon-opencode decision-router help
npx pantheon-opencode decision-router setup-model opencode-console-jev/jev-1.13 --monthly-usd 5 --per-decision-usd 0.10
npx pantheon-opencode decision-router doctor
npx pantheon-opencode decision-router status [--target <dir>]
npx pantheon-opencode decision-router setup [--apply] [--json] [--target <dir>] [--selection <value>] [--accept-migration]
npx pantheon-opencode decision-router preview
npx pantheon-opencode decision-router select openai-decisions/gpt-6-luna
npx pantheon-opencode decision-router enable openai-decisions gpt-6-luna
npx pantheon-opencode decision-router enable
npx pantheon-opencode decision-router consent yes
npx pantheon-opencode decision-router caps user --monthly-usd 5 --per-decision-usd 0.10
npx pantheon-opencode decision-router caps provider openai-decisions --monthly-usd 5 --per-decision-usd 0.10
npx pantheon-opencode decision-router caps model openai-decisions gpt-6-luna --monthly-usd 5 --per-decision-usd 0.10
npx pantheon-opencode decision-router period confirm --current none --next 2026-10
npx pantheon-opencode decision-router holds
npx pantheon-opencode decision-router holds release --provider <dead-provider> --reason "<why>"

help, status, setup/preview and holds are read-only: they do not create, migrate, or write the config or the SQLite ledger. They open the ledger through a separate read-only surface (node:sqlite with readOnly: true), so an absent database stays absent and an unknown schema is reported instead of being migrated. holds never reserves, reconciles, releases, or prunes — with one deliberate exception: holds release --provider <p> --reason "<why>" is the administrative correction for dead routes only. A provider that no longer exists in the route catalog can never reconcile its holds, so they would freeze budget forever; release archives every pending/uncertain hold of that provider into the ledger's released_holds audit table (schema v4) with the mandatory reason and frees the reserved budget. A live catalog provider is refused — its holds settle by reconciliation or roll off with the period. Earlier revisions opened the ledger for write from status and holds; that is fixed here and pinned by tests.

select records a preference and nothing else: it never enables the router, never records consent, never opens the ledger, and never changes which candidates are enabled. Moving the selection to a different provider/model revokes the consent recorded for the previous target, because that consent did not cover the new one. Selecting the same target again leaves consent untouched.

docs.title: Computed artifact preview (not a change plan)
docs.text:
setup prints a diff of the artifacts this layer owns, and preview is the same command with --apply refused:

  • the user-level config $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/pantheon/decision-router.json;
  • with --target <dir>, that target's .pantheon/install-state.json when it already exists (no state is ever fabricated for an unmanaged target).

The comparison is content-based, using the snapshot method of the idempotency probe: lstat + SHA-256 + size + mode of the current file against the exact bytes the writer would produce (preview and writer share one serializer). Each artifact is therefore create (missing), unchanged (same hash) or update (different hash), and changed fields are listed by name with the value of an allowlisted set of activation flags only — never file contents or hashes.

This deliberately is not the installer's "Change plan". A measured second idempotent apply announced 112 create and created nothing, because the announcement described what writers were asked to do rather than what the target bytes are. The property a test pins here is the opposite: preview → --apply → preview reports 0 create · 0 update, and a byte-level edit flips exactly the field that changed. --apply re-reads every artifact first and refuses the whole plan if anything moved since the preview.

--accept-migration exists for one case only: rewriting a legacy-schema config that would migrate to enabled: true. Without the flag the plan is BLOCKED and nothing is written, so a preview/apply can never activate turn selection as a side effect.

docs.title: No extra backup, and why that matters
docs.text: Installer backup sets accumulate one directory per application and contain credential-bearing material (API keys/tokens) by the installer's own log. The decision-layer setup path creates no backup and no copy: it writes only the artifacts in the preview and says so in its output.

docs.title: Install-state consistency
docs.text:
.pantheon/install-state.json keeps a target-specific preference record (provider, egress_consent). It is not runtime authority. Its only legal value is the projection of the user-level config (projectDecisionRouterInstallState), so the two surfaces cannot disagree about consent: the record never asserts consent the config does not have. status --target <dir> reports consistent or the exact divergent fields, and setup --target <dir> --apply reconciles them without touching updated_at. typesafe-jev is accepted as a canonical provider id so a projected record survives a read/write round trip instead of resetting to Local.

File-ownership tracking is partial and asymmetric: file_inventory holds 53 of 106 project artifacts and 0 of 107 global artifacts, and it covers neither opencode.json nor AGENTS.md. This preview therefore makes no claim about "everything the installer owns"; it compares the decision-layer artifacts.

Legacy provider/model selection, consent, caps, and period commands only manage stored administrative state. They do not authorize or activate a production provider request. The manual pantheon_local_decision tool remains local: it does not read provider credentials, reserve provider usage, or call Fetch. The historical canary and test records describe old adapter assumptions only; they do not establish a current host permission contract, provider eligibility, or egress safety.

docs.title: Historical provider eligibility, payload, protocol, and ledger (removed)
docs.text:
Provider/model eligibility tables, endpoint and payload descriptions, pricing, permission assertions, and admission/reconciliation requirements from previous revisions are historical documentation, not a current runtime contract. The direct-fetch provider adapter, its payload protocol, and the fetch-path usage verifier were removed from source; the ledger remains and now settles the native route from host-reported cost. Nothing in the package performs a Pantheon-owned provider request.

There is no active per-turn provider allowlist or route in this subsystem. The explicit pantheon_jev_decide tool is the only native egress surface; it is invoked on demand, never in the background, and carries its own consent, budget, and permission chain. Do not rely on old caps, consent flags, permission checks, or secret-pattern filters as an egress or payload-safety boundary beyond that tool. Any future per-turn wiring requires a new consent/payload policy, proven current-turn correlation, spend/overshoot controls, Themis review, and explicit approval. Native Decisions status is documented in V2 native Decisions.

docs.title: Measured coverage and unmeasured surfaces (decision layer)
docs.text:
The registry reports coverage as measured, premise, advisory, or deferred, and measured never means "effect measured". What that means in practice: P7 and P8 are wired behind flags (both off by default), P1 and P2 are wired in shadow at the prompt hook, P3 is wired in shadow at its declared tool.invoke, P9 is wired in shadow on the measured compaction carrier, P11 is wired in shadow inside ctx.tool.transform, and P4, P5, P6 and P10 are library code with no production call site:

The local per-turn recommendation marker described above is separate from these P1/P2 shadow telemetry points; its advisory effect does not activate or strengthen those decision-layer points.

Point Surface Status What is NOT covered P1 (agent), P2 (skill) session.hook('prompt') Registered in shadow: they observe a content-free projection of the admission payload and record effect: none. P2 is advisory only — an empirical no-op on the default path, because the host sends prompt.skills absent. No effect was measured, and records are in-memory and unread in production (test-visible only). P1 activation still waits on PM-07. P2b filtering was cancelled by measurement, not emulated; no token reduction is claimed. P3 (complexity) tool.invoke Registered in shadow at pantheon_local_decision: the tool hands the adapter its own input, which carries complexity and gateStatus, so it classifies when invoked and applies nothing. No tool call was ever measured (PM-09), and records are in-memory and unread in production. P7 (loop) session.execution.succeeded Behind PANTHEON_V2_P7_LOOP, off by default. The 12-execution cap (P7_LOOP_MAX_EXECUTIONS) is advisory: reset() is caller-supplied, no measured host surface signals a user turn, and the streak is not claimed to reset on any event. Effect is none and unmeasured (C6 is closed by PROBE-E; no P7 effect was observed); nested depth ≥ 2, failed/interrupted child executions and image jobs were not exercised. Never describe this as working loop enforcement. P9 (compaction) session.hook('compaction') Registered in shadow on the measured carrier: the top-level sessionID and the system part array. The record carries the decision key and the payload shape; nothing is pushed, so the injected context is unchanged. Measured on top-level and child sessions: PROBE-G fired the hook in a real child 3/3 with the child's sessionID at top level and the same 7-key payload (system array of 4), so there is no child-specific branch. reason: "overflow" was not inducible in 6 error shapes (PROBE-G §3.2) and its carrier is UNKNOWN; the checkpoint summary/reinjection inside a child was not exercised; the messages channel remains UNKNOWN. A payload whose only id is a nested session.id produces no decision, and no measured surface carries the memory candidate list, so the record names that absence and claims no retention or priority. P11 (catalog) tool.transform Registered in shadow inside the ctx.tool.transform callback: it reads the draft the host hands it and calls none of its mutators. Shadow has no responder, so the record is the validated choice question over the draft ids (catalog.no.answer), never a selection. ctx.model/ctx.provider were not exercised as catalogue sources (PM-08), and no host catalogue (ctx.catalog) exists at any measured point. P8 (guardrail) permission.evaluate Not activatable by measurement; recorded as advisory, starts off and never shadow. PROBE-F delivered 24 real events and measured delivery, payload, order and write honouring — but no declared rule matched any payload (valid action token, sessionID always present), an unrecognised effect is resolved as ask and executed, and permission.evaluate.egress is unreachable. The current rule set narrows nothing. P8 itself was never enabled, so no narrowing was observed; the inert verdict comes from the measured payload matched against the declared rules. execute.before remains the only hard barrier (a throw there denies; a throw in permission.evaluate does not).

P6 and P10 are unwired: they declared the prompt hook, but that payload carries neither council candidates nor counsellor claims, so constructing them there would only record a permanent refusal. P4 and P5 are unwired for the same reason: the measured context payload carries system text parts and no memory candidate array for P4 to rank, and the execute.after event carries no declared { requirements, responses } pair for P5 to verify.

Budget facts are the same story: caps are local admission controls computed from explicit configuration, and they are not invoice guarantees. There are no default caps, no automatic period rollover, and no admission from a missing ledger.

docs.title: Offline harness calibration (run 2026-10-31)
docs.text:
The registry above records what each point is; this section records what the offline harness actually exercised. It is a contract calibration, not a performance benchmark.

Field Recorded value Command npx tsx tests/pantheon/v2-decision-harness.test.ts Runtime Node 26.4.0, no provider, no network, synthetic fixtures Result exit 0 — V2 decision harness: 264 cases (132 normal, 66 refusal, 66 adversarial) across 11 points Per point 24 cases: 12 normal, 6 refusal, 6 adversarial; the suite asserts ≥ 20 total, ≥ 5 refusal and ≥ 5 adversarial per point Pass rate 264/264 cases passed; the script exits non-zero on the first failed assertion

What the 264 cases check: policy admission per declared mode and status (shadow admitted with effect: none, off and migration points never admitted as shadow, deferred never admitted), deterministic replay, shadow no-op including a mutation attempted inside the isolated payload, the telemetry allowlist under hostile field names and injected secrets, budget exhaustion, closed gates, unknown points, the ask/rank/verify contracts and their refusals, the frozen registry against tampering, consumption of session.execution.succeeded from the measured envelope fixture, and an offline assertion that no v2-decision-* module references node:http, node:https, node:net, undici, fetch or Bifrost.

Refusal behaviour is a pass, not an error, and it is asserted in the 66 refusal cases: an unknown point returns UNKNOWN_POINT; an exhausted budget returns BUDGET_EXHAUSTED; a closed gate returns GATE_CLOSED; malformed telemetry is rejected; a primitive that answers refusal is accepted as a success while a missing answer is FAILED_TO_RESPOND; mandatory verification without a verdict is BLOCK, and optional verification with only a confidence value is FAIL; rank with no candidates returns NO_CANDIDATES and duplicate ids return DUPLICATE_ID; the heuristic returns refusal rather than inventing a winner.

Not measured by this harness — no claim may be derived from it: token counts, token savings, answer quality, latency or cost; any effect inside a host turn (effect remains unmeasured for every point, and P7 records effect: 'none'); permission.evaluate delivery, payload shape or write honouring; and the embeddings-versus-BM25 comparison, which is not run (offline environment, no embedding model), leaving BM25 as the baseline with no numeric result in either direction.

docs.title: Loading the standalone export
docs.text:
pantheon-opencode/local-decision-router resolves to src/pantheon/local-decision-router.ts — TypeScript source, not JavaScript. It loads inside the OpenCode host, which transpiles package exports, or under an explicit transpiler such as tsx:

npx tsx -e "import('pantheon-opencode/local-decision-router').then((m) => console.log(Object.keys(m)))"

Plain Node cannot import TypeScript from node_modules and fails with ERR_UNSUPPORTED_NODE_MODULES_TYPE_STRIPPING, so this subpath is not a plain-Node JavaScript entry point. The published CLI avoids it by importing a committed ESM ledger bundle; the build command and drift gate live in CONTRIBUTING.

import { recommendLocalDecision } from 'pantheon-opencode/local-decision-router'

const recommendation = recommendLocalDecision({
  schemaVersion: 1,
  domains: ['hermes'],
  complexity: {
    boundedness: 0,
    reversibility: 0,
    dependencies: 0,
    uncertainty: 0,
    verification: 0,
  },
  gateStatus: 'none',
})

docs.title: Input and route behavior
docs.text:
Each complexity dimension is 0..2 where higher = riskier / less contained: boundedness: 2 means POORLY bounded (not "very bounded"), and the aggregate label is max(dimensions) — one hot dimension labels the task high (lo 0,0,2,2,2 and hi 2,2,0,0,0 are both high by design).

Input schema version 1 accepts only structured fields: domains, complexity, and gateStatus. Extra fields (including free-form task text) make the input invalid; the router does not parse text, infer keywords, or call a model.

domains contains exact canonical specialist role IDs from Pantheon's existing agent set, not newly invented aliases. Exactly one allowlisted specialist ID produces a route recommendation; an empty, unknown, unsupported, or multi-role domain abstains. zeus is not a routable target. These IDs are advisory labels; the host's existing dispatch remains authoritative.

The result includes schemaVersion, policyVersion, decision (route or abstain), agent (null on abstention), and a stable reasonCode. Complexity is reported independently in complexity.label and complexity.reasonCode.

docs.title: Structured complexity and gates
docs.text:
Each of the five dimensions—boundedness, reversibility, dependencies, uncertainty, and verification—must be an integer from 0 to 2, following the proposed dimension definitions in the offline evaluation protocol. The classification is deterministic: all zeroes yield low; any 1 and no 2 yields medium; any 2 yields high. Missing, malformed, or out-of-range dimensions yield abstain for complexity.

gateStatus is carried separately as none, review_required, human_approval_required, or unresolved. It is not a complexity dimension: a low complexity label cannot clear, reduce, or replace a security, data-integrity, review, or authorization gate. Invalid gate values become unresolved and cause the overall decision to abstain (agent: null). Invalid complexity dimensions also abstain before routing; malformed input or internal validation failures never produce a route recommendation.

docs.title: Pantheon Model Routing — Deep Analysis with Per-Plan Fallback Chains
docs.text:
V2 runtime note (2026-10): The static model tables and presets in this document describe legacy V1 routing analysis; they do not select models in OpenCode V2. V2 leaves the host's model intact unless an explicit overrides.agents.<agent>.model is configured. Only that agent's manual model and optional variant are applied by the V2 agent transform. Legacy preset markers in active-preset.json and PANTHEON_MODEL_PRESET are ignored, not deleted, and do not activate a provider or model. V2 has no model wizard or implicit model selection. The V1 legacy path is frozen for this beta: it keeps its legacy behavior and static routing.yml preset IDs, and the V1 preset migration is not authorized in this beta. V2 manual overrides and status are project-only; global override files are not read or applied. The V2 tool rejects global set/reset and same-call confirm/authorize_global flags because it has no independent user-approval API. Global overrides require separate explicit human authorization in a future surface and are not currently supported. pantheon_model status reports configuration, not which model served a completion, and is the user-accessible place to see override warnings. If an override is invalid or malformed, V2 preserves the host model and records an internal diagnostic; the user must call pantheon_model status to see the warning. The V2 server plugin has no documented toast or other proactive user-visible notification API during transform, so no toast/proactive warning is promised. V1 behavior remains legacy and unchanged.

docs.title: Token-Based Pricing Strategy
docs.text: We are token-based. Every API call costs per input + output token. For coding: deepseek-v4-flash (SWE-bench 79%, $0.28/1M) is sufficient — 89x cheaper than Opus. For reasoning: quality matters — use best available. Fallback chains use ONLY models available in the same plan — no cross-plan mixing.
